applies_when: the trainer host is shared and other tenants can claim a GPU at any time, which is its steady state -- 6 of 8 GPUs carried foreign compute apps at 2026-08-18T14:58Z
diagnosis: A foreign tenant held or reclaimed GPU 5 while our trainer was resident, so the two runs shared SM and memory bandwidth with someone else's job. That is exactly the condition the co-tenancy check exists to catch, and it caught it: the check behaved correctly and the two records are correctly excluded from the band. What remains uncertain is whether the lower step counts were caused by the co-tenant or merely correlate with it, because host CPU load was also drifting over the same interval and step count on this benchmark is CPU-bound; a single voided pair cannot separate those two explanations.

applies_when: the dispatcher selects GPUs by an instantaneous memory poll on a shared host, i.e. as long as host/dispatch.py picks free_gpus from a single nvidia-smi snapshot with no memory of prior invalidations
diagnosis: The dispatcher's free-GPU test is instantaneous: memory.used <= MINFREE_MB at the moment of the poll. A GPU whose tenant is between jobs passes that test and then reclaims memory seconds later. Nothing in the loop remembers that this GPU already destroyed a run, so the same device was picked again and cost a second 300-second budget plus ~210s of startup. The competing explanation -- that the second co-tenancy was independent bad luck rather than the same tenant cycling -- is not ruled out by two events, but the cost of assuming independence is one voided run each time and the cost of assuming otherwise is only a GPU we skip while others are free.
mitigation: Quarantine a GPU that has just invalidated one of our runs: in host/dispatch.py, record the device uuid on every CO-TENANT event and exclude that uuid from free_gpus for a cooldown period, so a device whose tenant is cycling cannot burn a second and third run. This must be enforced in code -- the previous occurrence cost two runs precisely because the rule existed nowhere.
observation: After C01_control was voided by a co-tenant on gpu5, the dispatcher launched C02_control onto gpu5 again 10 minutes later and it was co-tenanted within 11 seconds (dispatch.log 12:37:49Z LAUNCH, 12:38:00Z CO-TENANT). Both runs were then lost. The four runs that survived went to gpu1. At 2026-08-18T14:58Z gpu5 still carried a foreign compute app holding 80499 MiB.

applies_when: the dispatcher groups queue entries by wave_group to decide what launches together, i.e. for as long as yoked pairs are the measurement design
diagnosis: next_batch() built its wave groups from the RUNNABLE set, which excludes entries that already carry a claim directory. A wave therefore only had to be intact within a single dispatcher pass; once any member was claimed, the remainder re-presented itself as a smaller, complete-looking wave and became eligible to launch. The atomicity that claim_all() enforces within one pass was silently absent across passes. The competing explanation -- that the four entries were never all present in the host queue at once -- is ruled out: all four carry wave_group 'W03a' in queue.json and were merged to the host in the same tick. For a control block the consequence is only untidiness, since every control is byte-identical; for a treatment it would silently dissolve the treatment-vs-control pairing that is the sole reason a wave_group exists, and the resulting comparison would be cross-wave drift wearing the label of a paired result.
mitigation: host/dispatch.py now sizes a wave from wave_sizes(), counting the members the wave was QUEUED with rather than the members still unclaimed, and refuses to launch any group whose runnable count is short of that, logging 'WAVE SPLIT'. tests/test_wave_launch.py case 5b reproduces the exact failure -- two survivors of a four-member wave -- and asserts they do not launch while an intact four-member wave still does.
observation: W03a was queued as ONE wave_group of four byte-identical controls (W03a_1..W03a_4). At 2026-08-18T15:24:11Z the dispatcher launched only W03a_1_control on gpu6 and W03a_2_control on gpu7, leaving W03a_3 and W03a_4 unclaimed in the queue. applies_when: the dispatcher can be restarted while trainers it did not start are still alive -- which is every restart, since trainers are deliberately detached so a dispatcher crash does not kill a run mid-flight
diagnosis: A trainer spends roughly its first 200 seconds tokenizing on the CPU and allocates no GPU memory in that window, so `memory.used <= MINFREE_MB` reports its GPU as free. The dispatcher's only other guard is `g not in running`, which is in-memory state a restart destroys, while the trainers themselves survive because they are launched with start_new_session=True. So the window between killing a dispatcher and its children finishing is a window in which a fresh dispatcher will double-book every GPU that is still in CPU startup. The singleton lock does not help: it prevents two dispatchers, not a new dispatcher plus an old dispatcher's orphans.
mitigation: host/dispatch.py now writes work/<name>/launch.json at launch (pid, gpu, uuid, slot, cores) and calls adopt_running() at startup, which re-attaches every claimed run that has a work dir, no result and a live pid -- so a restarted dispatcher counts those GPUs as occupied and finishes those runs normally. Independently, the co-tenancy check now also fires when more than one of OUR OWN processes holds a device, so if double-booking ever happens again the affected runs are marked invalid instead of silently entering the band.
observation: Restarting the dispatcher at 2026-08-18T15:33:42Z put a second pair of OUR trainers onto gpu6 and gpu7 while an earlier pair was still resident. nvidia-smi then showed two of our pids on each device (4105709+4106607 on GPU-7533cdca, 4105710+4106608 on GPU-f6cb0281). The co-tenancy check did not fire, because it tests `owner != me` and every one of those processes was ours. All four runs would have been written ok:true and entered the control band. They were killed and their claims, work directories and results removed before any of them completed.

applies_when: runs complete more than one epoch of the fixed dataset -- check final_epoch on the yoked control of the SAME wave rather than assuming, because this is set by host load and can revert without warning
diagnosis: Host CPU contention, not anything in the model, sets step count on this benchmark, and it moved enough to change the regime rather than merely the noise. At the current load the 300-second budget completes TWO passes over the fixed data instead of one, so the second half of every run is repeated tokens; and the CPU-side loader share fell from about 93% to about 66%. The campaign's written cost model -- that roughly 90% of the 300 seconds is the frozen single-threaded packing loop, so GPU FLOPs are near free and CPU work is near fatal -- was measured in the first regime and does not describe the second. It remains true that loader_frac and fwdbwd_frac are CPU wall-clock fractions around asynchronous CUDA launches, so neither number establishes how busy the GPU is; what is unambiguous is final_epoch, which is a counter emitted by the frozen loader. Whether an intervention that helps under one pass also helps under two is untested here, and the epoch boundary is a plausible moderator for anything touching memorization or capacity.
mitigation: Every proposal must state which regime it expects to act in and read final_epoch off its own wave's control rather than off the campaign's prose. Cross-block comparison is invalid on top of the wave-drift problem: C03-C06 and W02-W03 differ by an entire epoch of data exposure, so their val_bpb gap of roughly 0.014 is a regime difference, not an improvement anyone produced. tools/direction.py now prints the MEASURED regime -- step range, final_epoch values and loader_frac range recomputed from results -- above the DIRECTION SPACE table, so a council round reads the operating point it is actually in instead of a hardcoded belief about it.
observation: The four sequential controls C03-C06 ran 621-815 steps, all reporting final_epoch 1.0, loader_frac 0.925-0.936 and mfu 25.8-34.0. The eight concurrent controls W02a/W02b/W02c/W03a ran 1010-1021 steps, all reporting final_epoch 2.0, loader_frac 0.661-0.673 and mfu 42.2-42.7. Same frozen prepare.py, same byte-identical variant 7d538ad931e1.py, same 300-second budget. Host load average moved from roughly 180 to roughly 15-17 on 192 cores between the two blocks.

applies_when: a wave assigns its members to different dispatcher slots, which is every yoked pair -- and it binds for as long as the fix is counterbalancing rather than a demonstrated repair of the underlying asymmetry
diagnosis: The two taskset core blocks are not interchangeable: cores 108-119 execute the frozen single-threaded packing loop about 2.43 ms per step faster than cores 96-107, most plausibly a NUMA or core-topology asymmetry on a 192-core host. That yields 8.7 extra steps in the fixed 300-second budget, and the campaign's own step law (-0.0687 bpb per e-fold of steps) converts 1019.3/1010.6 into a predicted 0.00059 bpb -- which matches the measured 0.000499 closely enough that step count alone explains the slot effect. The competing explanation, that the two physical GPUs differ, is not separable from the core blocks by these runs alone because slot, GPU and core block moved together in every wave; distinguishing them requires deliberately crossing GPU against core block, and for the purpose of this lesson it does not matter which is responsible, because slot assignment carries both.
mitigation: COUNTERBALANCE THE SLOT. Every treatment-versus-control comparison must be run as two waves with the slot order swapped -- wave A queued [treatment, control], wave B queued [control, treatment] -- because the dispatcher assigns slots to a wave's members in queue order. The two waves' deltas are then averaged, which cancels a fixed slot offset exactly. A single yoked pair is NOT sufficient: the offset is 0.000499 against a measured band of 0.00071, so an uncounterbalanced pair can manufacture or erase an effect of exactly the size this campaign is hunting, depending only on which slot the treatment happened to land in. Do not subtract an estimated offset instead: the campaign's rule is that raw val_bpb is the verdict, and a counterbalanced design removes the bias by construction rather than by a fitted correction. Note also that the reported within-wave band of 0.00071 is mostly THIS BIAS rather than random error -- the sd of the paired difference is 0.000131, so a counterbalanced design resolves effects roughly five times smaller than the raw band suggests.
observation: Across all 7 concurrent control waves (W02a, W02b, W02c, W03a, W04a, W04b, W04c), the member launched into dispatcher slot 0 (gpu6, taskset cores 96-107) had a WORSE val_bpb than the member in slot 1 (gpu7, cores 108-119) in 7 of 7 waves, with no exceptions. Paired delta gpu6 minus gpu7 = +0.000499, sd of the paired difference 0.000131. Slot 0 averaged 1010.6 steps at step_ms_med 299.97; slot 1 averaged 1019.3 steps at step_ms_med 297.54. Every one of these 14 runs used the byte-identical control variant 7d538ad931e1.py.

applies_when: polar_express_coeffs has a fixed length and the Newton-Schulz loop slices it by ns_steps -- i.e. until the coefficient table is extended or the slice is replaced by a repeat
diagnosis: Slicing a fixed-length list saturates silently. Python returns the whole list for any index at or above its length, so the ns axis is real only over 1..5 and is a no-op above it. A queued ns=6 or ns=8 arm would consume a 300-second slot plus startup, produce a result record labelled `knob:ns` that the policy counts as a genuine run against that axis, and report a val_bpb drawn from the control distribution -- so it would look like a small null, advance the axis dry-streak toward closing an axis that was never actually varied, and pollute a comparison as a treatment that is mathematically a control. The competing explanation, that such a run is harmlessly redundant, is wrong for exactly that accounting reason.
mitigation: make_variant.build() now raises VariantEditError for ns above the coefficient-table length, so the entry dies at queue time rather than on a GPU at 3am. Independently, three registered claims measured at exactly 124M agree that 5 iterations is already the plateau and that raising it does not improve final loss, so the upward direction of this axis has no evidential support either. Only ns in 1..4 is a real experiment.
observation: baseline/train.py:304 defines polar_express_coeffs with exactly 5 entries, and lines 334 and 339 iterate `polar_express_coeffs[:ns_steps]`. Building variants across ns shows ns=6, ns=8 and ns=20 each produce a DIFFERENT source file with a different content hash (fcbde4c14189.py, 50a3b303aa48.py, c992ba0844a5.py) while executing the identical 5 iterations as the control 7d538ad931e1.py. queue_from_round.py's byte-identical guard compares generated SOURCE against the control's source, and the source genuinely differs, so such an entry passes the door.

applies_when: runs are launched into fixed dispatcher slots with a stable per-slot offset, and any document quotes a single number as the campaign's resolution
diagnosis: Both errors run in the flattering direction, which is the specific drift the numeric registry exists to catch and did not: a best-versus-best gap sounds like a smaller regime confound than the mean gap really is, and a band inflated by a fixed slot effect makes the instrument look coarser than it is while making any future effect that clears it look more impressive. The band figure is not wrong as computed -- it is 2x the mean WITHIN-WAVE sd and each wave straddles both slots -- it is wrong as INTERPRETED, because it pools a removable fixed effect with random error and then gets quoted as a resolution limit. The competing explanation for the low within-slot sd, that slot 0 and slot 1 runs are somehow correlated within a wave, is ruled out by the fact that the two slots' sds are computed across DIFFERENT waves spanning an hour of host-load drift.
mitigation: Quote three numbers, never one. The WITHIN-WAVE band 0.000661 is what an uncounterbalanced pair must clear. The COUNTERBALANCED resolution 2 x 0.000130 / sqrt(2) = 0.000184 is what a slot-swapped two-wave design achieves, and it agrees with the pooled within-slot floor of 0.000187 computed a completely different way -- two independent routes to the same number, which is why it should be trusted. The regime gap between the 1-epoch and 2-epoch blocks is 0.023913 on block means; do not quote 0.014560 without saying it is best-versus-best. Retire the '70% of the band' phrasing entirely: it is 1/sqrt(2) and carries no information.
observation: An independent Fable audit recomputed two figures this campaign had been quoting and found both wrong. (1) L005_operating_point_moved describes 'their val_bpb gap of roughly 0.014' between the 1-epoch and 2-epoch control blocks. The block MEAN gap is 1.015288 minus 0.991374 = 0.023913 over 4 and 18 valid runs; 0.014560 is the BEST-versus-BEST gap, a different and more flattering statistic than the sentence implies. (2) The campaign has been quoting a noise band of 0.00066 as its resolution floor. Pooling the 18 wave-control runs WITHIN each dispatcher slot gives sd 0.0000903 for cores 96-107 and 0.0000963 for cores 108-119, pooled 0.0000933, so the genuine random-noise floor is 2 sd = 0.000187. The audit also showed the 'slot bias is 70% of the band' framing is the algebraic identity 1/sqrt(2), which holds for ANY set of paired deltas that all share a sign, and is therefore not a measurement at all.

applies_when: the local queue is the authoring surface and a sync ships it to the host, i.e. for as long as experiments are staged locally and executed remotely
diagnosis: tools/tick.sh merged the local queue into the host queue by NAME ONLY -- `new = [e for e in inc if e['name'] not in have]` -- so an entry that already existed on the host was never updated again. Every later correction to an existing entry was silently discarded at the sync boundary while both queues reported the same entry count, and the local file showed the corrected values. The consequence was not hypothetical: the precond arms, which are the round's actual hypothesis, were queued to run a variant with no activation diagnostic and no hypothesis_id, so coe.py E3 would have skipped them and the run would have been INCONCLUSIVE by construction after spending four 300-second slots. The competing explanation -- that the dispatcher copied a stale file -- is ruled out by the host's variant file containing the print while the queue pointed elsewhere.
mitigation: tools/tick.sh now updates entries that already exist on the host instead of only appending new names, and reports 'N added, M updated in place' so a silent no-op is visible. Entries that have already RUN or been CLAIMED are deliberately left untouched, because rewriting a launched entry would misdescribe a run whose result is already on disk. Verification rule for the future: after correcting a queue entry, read the field back FROM THE HOST before letting it launch -- the local file agreeing with itself proves nothing about what will execute.

applies_when: the current dispatcher, variant generator and yoked-pair design are in use; a structural change to any of them retires this validation and requires a fresh positive control
diagnosis: The measurement chain detects a real effect of the size the literature predicted, so it is not null-generating. That matters because before this run every one of the campaign's 24 completed runs was a control, the counterbalanced design had never been exercised, and the harness had produced six silent instrumentation defects in a day -- so a null from any treatment would have been uninterpretable, indistinguishable from a pipeline that cannot register a difference. Two secondary confirmations came free. The slot offset held at 10 of 10 same sign including a wave where the TREATMENT sat in slot 1, so the offset is a property of the slot rather than of what runs on it, which is what L006 asserts. And the effect was larger in the wave where the treatment sat in the SLOWER slot, so an uncounterbalanced single pair would have mis-estimated it in a direction that depends only on where the arm landed.
mitigation: Nulls measured under this harness may now be read as evidence rather than as possible instrument failure -- but only for effects at or above the counterbalanced resolution of 0.000174, and only for comparisons that are actually counterbalanced. Re-run a positive control after any change to dispatch.py, make_variant.py's shared instrumentation, or the wave design, because this validation is of the CHAIN and not of any single component.
observation: The ns=3 arm, queued explicitly as a POSITIVE CONTROL rather than a SOTA candidate, produced val_bpb 0.994190 in dispatcher slot 0 against its yoked control's 0.991096 (delta +0.003094), and 0.993713 in slot 1 against its yoked control's 0.991517 (delta +0.002196). The counterbalanced mean of those two within-wave deltas is +0.002645 against a counterbalanced resolution of 0.000174 -- 15x the resolution, same sign in both waves, with the treatment occupying opposite slots. Both waves finished at final_epoch 2.0 on both arms.

applies_when: the model is ~124M parameters with 512-wide Muon matrices and a step time around 300ms, so the polar iteration is a fraction of a percent of the step
diagnosis: At 124M parameters the Muon matrices are 512-wide, and the whole orthogonalization is a small enough share of a 297ms step that removing 40% of its iterations is invisible in wall clock. The trade the direction was premised on -- spend orthogonalization fidelity, buy steps -- does not exist at this operating point, because there is nothing meaningful to buy. This is consistent with three registered claims that 5 iterations is already the plateau at exactly this scale, and it converts them from imported priors into a measurement on this system. The competing explanation, that the loss came from something other than the reduced iteration count, is weak: the variant differs from the control only in the ns_steps literal, and the effect reproduced across both slots.
mitigation: Do not spend further slots reducing ns to reclaim FLOPs: the measured saving is ~0.2% of step time against a break-even of about 1.25%, so the arithmetic cannot close even if the loss cost were zero, and it is not zero. blocks_values forbids ns below 5 as well as at or above the coefficient-table length, leaving no runnable value on this axis -- which is the honest state of it: the axis is measured, not merely untried.
observation: Reducing Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 3 cost +0.002645 bpb as a counterbalanced mean, and bought essentially no throughput: step_ms_med was 299.45 for the treatment versus 300.01 for the control in slot 0, and 296.57 versus 297.29 in slot 1 -- about 0.2% of step time. Step counts were 1013 vs 1020 and 1022 vs 1011, i.e. the treatment did not gain steps.

applies_when: host/dispatch.py imports a policy module that also exists locally and is edited locally, which is true of direction.py and of anything it imports
diagnosis: host/dispatch.py imports direction.py FROM THE HOST, so the policy the dispatcher applies is whatever copy sits beside it, and nothing in the sync ships that file -- tick.sh pushes the queue, the variants and the gate verdict, and nothing else. The damage here was limited to a wrong log label, and only because is_platform() fails safe on any unrecognised key: had it defaulted the other way, a treatment carrying an unknown key would have been labelled a control, exempted from the decision cutoff, and pooled into the very control block that measures the noise band. That is the exact failure the fail-safe clause in is_platform was written to prevent, and this run is the first time it actually fired in anger. The band itself is computed locally, so no measurement was corrupted.
mitigation: direction.py is now shipped to the host and verified by md5 against the local copy (f9f9d1bf1739e0e4a303884f27165df8 on both). Standing rule: after registering a new axis or mechanism in tools/direction.py, ship it before the first entry using it can launch, and confirm with the host's own label() rather than the local one. The deeper protection is already in place and should not be weakened -- is_platform() refusing to call ANY config with an unrecognised key a control is what kept this to a cosmetic defect.
observation: The dispatcher logged 'LAUNCH precond_pre_slot0 gpu6 cores=96-107 [control] wave=R1P_A' -- labelling a mechanism arm as a control. The host's copy of direction.py carried MECHANISMS = ('mtp','unet','zloss','noqknorm','prefetch'), without 'precond', because the mechanism was registered in the local copy and the local copy was never shipped. On the host, label() therefore returned 'control' while is_platform() returned False, since unknown_keys() saw {'precond'} and failed safe.

applies_when: the dispatcher assigns slots from free capacity rather than pinning a wave to named cores, and more than two GPUs can be free at once
diagnosis: The counterbalanced design cancels a FIXED OFFSET BETWEEN TWO SPECIFIC CORE BLOCKS by running the treatment on each of them in turn. It silently assumed the dispatcher would give both waves of a twin the same two slots, which it does not guarantee: slots are assigned from whatever is free, so a twin launched when more GPUs are available lands on a different pair. Averaging a delta measured on pair A with a delta measured on pair B does not cancel anything -- it adds an unmeasured offset to a measured one, and the result would have been reported as a counterbalanced verdict. The analysis code made the same assumption in a second place, collapsing the core block to a 0/1 index by testing whether the first core number was below 108, which maps BOTH new blocks to 1 and would have shown the twin as 'treatment in slot 1 twice' rather than as a different experiment.
mitigation: tools/verdict.py now keys an arm by its actual taskset core block rather than a 0/1 index, groups arms by the core-block PAIR they ran on, and will only average deltas within a pair where the treatment occupied both roles. A pair with no swap is reported as not counterbalanced instead of being pooled. The precond comparison is being re-run as R1P_C and R1P_D on the same 96-107/108-119 pair R1P_A used. The R1P_B runs are not discarded -- they are valid within-wave deltas on their own pair, and if they agree with the re-run that is independent corroboration on hardware whose bias was never measured. Note the ns=3 positive control is unaffected: both its waves used the 96-107/108-119 pair with the roles correctly swapped.
observation: R1P_A launched on cores 96-107 and 108-119. Minutes later, with four GPUs free, the dispatcher launched R1P_B concurrently onto cores 120-131 and 132-143. All 26 completed runs to that point had used only 96-107 and 108-119, so the relative bias of the second pair is entirely unmeasured. The two waves were queued as a slot-swapped counterbalanced pair for the precond hypothesis.

applies_when: an elementwise second moment is computed on a quantity whose scale differs by orders of magnitude from the one the buffer's floor and initialisation were chosen for
diagnosis: Moving the NorMuon block before the polar iteration makes it compute the second moment of the RAW MOMENTUM instead of the orthogonalized update. Raw momentum entries are orders of magnitude smaller, so the per-row mean square falls below the 1e-10 floor that clamp_min imposes on a zero-initialised buffer with 1-beta2=0.05 and no bias correction. Once clamped, step_size = buffer.clamp_min(1e-10).rsqrt() is a CONSTANT rather than a per-row quantity; final_scale then renormalizes by v_norm/v_norm_new, and the polar iteration's opening line X = X/(||X||*1.02+1e-6) divides out whatever global factor remains. The arm therefore ran as plain Muon minus NorMuon, not as input-side preconditioning, and its val_bpb bears on that accidental configuration rather than on the mechanism. The declared activation rule -- secmom_ortho_ratio below 0.1 -- PASSED, because the ratio correctly detected that the buffer had left orthogonalized scale; it could not detect that the buffer had fallen off the bottom instead. This is exactly the failure an independent Fable critic predicted before the run, in the words 'the clamp binds, the diagonal collapses to a constant, the polar normalization cancels it exactly, and the treatment silently becomes plain Muon-minus-NorMuon'; the campaign added secmom_clamp_frac because of that prediction, and it is the only reason this is visible.
mitigation: The precond result is INCONCLUSIVE about precond_before_ortho and must NOT be recorded as a negative: a non-activation says nothing about the mechanism. The mechanism needs re-implementing so the second moment is scale-appropriate for the momentum -- either normalize the momentum before taking its second moment, or replace the absolute clamp_min(1e-10) with a floor relative to the buffer's own mean, or add the bias correction the buffer lacks. An activation predicate needs BOTH a direction test and a degeneracy test: secmom_ortho_ratio proved the buffer left orthogonalized scale, and only secmom_clamp_frac revealed it had landed somewhere useless. Every future mechanism whose observable is a ratio should carry a companion observable for the floor, saturation or clamp that could make that ratio meaningless.
observation: Both precond arms emitted secmom_clamp_frac 0.99789 and 0.99791 -- 99.8% of the NorMuon second-moment buffer sat at the clamp_min(1e-10) floor -- against 0.00000 in all four yoked controls. secmom_rms was 1.59e-06 and 1.62e-06 for the treatments versus 3.22e-02 for the controls, and secmom_ortho_ratio was 2.4e-05 versus 4.86e-01. val_bpb was 0.992196 (slot 96-107, control 0.990908) and 0.992908 (slot 132-143, control 0.993341).

applies_when: prepare.py holds VOCAB_SIZE = 8192, which is frozen for this campaign
diagnosis: 124M is the parameter count of GPT-2 small at vocab 50257, which is what the upstream lineage of this benchmark uses; this fork retrains the tokenizer to 8192 and the figure was carried over without being recomputed. Two consequences follow and only the second is serious. First, every transfer score in the registry was assigned against a stated 124M rather than the true 50.33M; since the true model is SMALLER, a claim judged to transfer to 124M at ~1000 steps generally transfers at least as well to 50M, so the scores are conservative rather than inflated. Second, and materially, the vocabulary is 6.1x smaller than the papers most often used as comparators, which inverts the embedding accounting: value embeddings are 33% of all parameters here and wte+lm_head are only 17%, whereas at vocab 50257 the embedding tables dominate. Any claim about embedding learning rates, tied versus untied embeddings, vocabulary-scaled capacity, n-gram or memory tables, or the relative cost of the lm_head must be re-read against vocab 8192 before it is used, and several registered claims were scored without that context.
mitigation: State the operating point as ~50.3M parameters at vocab 8192, not 124M, in every future reader brief, council prompt and hypothesis. Value embeddings being a third of the parameter budget makes ve_placement a far larger lever than its two registered claims suggest, and makes any imported embedding-side result suspect until re-read at this vocabulary. Do not mass-rescore the existing registry: the scores are conservative in the direction that matters, and a blind rescore would be a fabrication. Re-read individually the claims whose effect depends on vocabulary size.
observation: baseline/prepare.py:45 sets VOCAB_SIZE = 8192. With n_embd 512, depth 8, mlp ratio 4 and the recorded n_ve_layers 4, the parameter count is wte 4.19M + lm_head 4.19M + value_embeds 16.78M + attention 8.39M + mlp 16.78M = 50.33M. The campaign's own KICKOFF.md, CLAUDE.md and every reader and council brief issued so far stated 124M. A mechanism-synthesis agent found the discrepancy independently and confirmed it by reproducing the recorded mfu_percent of 42.62 from the implied FLOPs per token to four significant figures.

applies_when: a mechanism branch exists in make_variant.py that no result record has ever exercised
diagnosis: Generator code written ahead of use is not exercised by anything: make_variant only proves an edit APPLIED, the tests check policy rather than observables, and no run had ever touched these branches. So defects sat in them indefinitely, and the campaign's own DIRECTION SPACE table ranked both as untouched high-priority work -- it would have spent slots on them and got inconclusive results. The common root with L014 is that an activation observable is itself an experiment that nobody had run: a treatment-only print cannot be wrong, a probe that saturates early measures the wrong phase, and a metric that improves for a reason unrelated to the mechanism will pass its own rule.
mitigation: Both branches are fixed: the qk statistic is now written into a preallocated device buffer every step with no host sync, emitted by EVERY variant including the control, and read once after the charged clock stops; mtp now also emits mtp_proj_rms, which is exactly zero at init so any non-zero value proves the optimizer used the new path. Standing rule: before a mechanism's first run, read its observable as if it were the hypothesis -- ask whether the control emits it, whether it could pass for a reason unrelated to the mechanism, and whether it saturates before the phase of interest. An observable is a measurement instrument and deserves the same scepticism as a result.
observation: Two mechanism branches that had never been executed were audited by hypothesis-authoring agents and each carried a defect that would have made its run uninterpretable. `noqknorm` appended to a Python list inside GPT.forward, which torch.compile must graph-break around; capped that list at 64 entries so the statistic described initialisation rather than end-of-run drift; and emitted the print only inside the treatment branch, so no control value existed to compare against. `mtp` emitted mtp_aux_loss_drop as its activation metric, but mtp_proj is zero-initialised and feeds the SHARED lm_head, so that metric falls as lm_head improves even if mtp_proj never leaves zero -- the arm would then be shifted label smoothing while the activation rule reported success.

applies_when: more than one of our trainers runs concurrently on this host, which is every wave wider than one
diagnosis: The per-slot penalty is not a fixed property of a core block; it grows with how many of OUR OWN trainers are running. Four concurrent trainers contend for shared host resources -- memory bandwidth and last-level cache being the obvious candidates on a 192-core box -- and the lowest core block suffers most, losing 40 steps relative to the highest. Two consequences follow. First, a wave's width is part of its operating point: a two-wide wave and a four-wide wave are not the same experiment, and a delta measured in one cannot be compared with a delta measured in the other any more than runs from different epochs could (L005_operating_point_moved_v2). Second, and counter-intuitively, using more of the four-GPU allocation makes the measurement WORSE: two-wide waves carry a 0.00047 offset while four-wide waves carry up to 0.00234 across slots. The competing explanation, that the four runs simply drifted with host load, is ruled out by the monotonicity in slot index and by step_ms_med tracking it exactly.
mitigation: Counterbalance within a pair AND at a fixed wave width; never average a delta from a two-wide wave with one from a four-wide wave. Prefer TWO-wide waves for any comparison whose expected effect is near the resolution, accepting the idle GPUs: the offset is roughly five times smaller and the counterbalanced residual sd is what actually sets what can be resolved. Reserve four-wide waves for screening effects an order of magnitude above the band, or for control waves like this one whose purpose is to measure the offsets themselves. This measurement also retro-explains an earlier run: the R1P_B precond arm sat on slot 3 against a control on slot 2, its observed delta was -0.000433, the slot-only prediction is -0.000433, and the residual attributable to the treatment is exactly 0.000000 -- an independent confirmation, from the apparatus rather than from the telemetry, that the arm never engaged.
observation: A four-wide wave of byte-identical controls (Q1a_s0..s3) gave val_bpb 0.993518, 0.992409, 0.991609, 0.991176 on cores 96-107, 108-119, 120-131, 132-143, with step counts 980, 999, 1010, 1020 and step_ms_med 309.46, 303.67, 300.07, 297.31. Both quantities are MONOTONE in slot index. The 96-107 minus 108-119 offset was +0.001109 here, against +0.000463 measured over nine TWO-wide waves. The spread across all four slots is 0.002342, which is 13x the counterbalanced resolution of 0.000174 and comparable to the entire measured ns=3 effect of +0.002645.

applies_when: the trainer host is shared, which is permanent; foreign tenants have taken between one and eight GPUs at various points in this campaign
diagnosis: This is the steady state of a shared box rather than a fault: the co-tenancy check and the quarantine both did exactly what they exist to do, and the visible cost was one wave. The interesting part is the magnitude of what was avoided. Those four runs lost about a quarter of their steps to contention, which the campaign's own step law converts to roughly 0.02 bpb -- more than a hundred times the counterbalanced resolution and larger than every effect measured so far combined. Had they entered the band or, worse, been paired against a treatment, they would have manufactured a result of arbitrary size. The competing explanation, that the step loss was ordinary host-load drift rather than the tenant, is ruled out by the timing: the CO-TENANT lines land within twelve seconds of one another and within three minutes of launch.
mitigation: No change to the checks, which worked. Two operational notes. First, a wave lost to co-tenancy costs the whole wave, so a four-wide design loses four runs where a two-wide loses two -- the wider design is more exposed as well as noisier (L017), and that is a second reason to prefer narrow waves for anything near the resolution. Second, quarantine state lives only in the dispatcher's memory, so restarting the dispatcher clears it: a restart during a tenant's cycle silently removes the protection. The quarantine is now lifted on EVIDENCE -- eight consecutive minutes with no foreign compute app on the device -- rather than by serving out a fixed timer, but persisting it across restarts remains open.
observation: At 2026-08-19T04:00:25Z through 04:00:37Z a foreign tenant acquired all four GPUs we were using, during the Q1b quad control wave. The dispatcher logged CO-TENANT on gpu4, gpu5, gpu6 and gpu7 in turn, marked Q1b_s0_control, Q1b_s1_control, Q1b_s2_control and Q1b_s3_control invalid, and quarantined every device for 45 minutes. The four runs completed with val_bpb 1.019584, 1.016201, 1.020391 and 1.016994 at 746, 761, 751 and 761 steps -- roughly 250 fewer steps than the same code achieved minutes earlier in Q1a, and all four are correctly excluded from every statistic by ok:false.

applies_when: the model is dense bf16 at this size on one H200 and mfu_percent sits in the 40s; a much smaller model or a much slower loader could genuinely idle the GPU and the pricing would have to be re-derived
diagnosis: The 'near-free' pricing came from reading loader_frac 0.66 to 0.93 as GPU idleness. CLAUDE.md warns in as many words that loader_frac and fwdbwd_frac are CPU wall-clock fractions measured around calls that launch ASYNCHRONOUS CUDA work, that fwdbwd_frac is kernel launch time rather than GPU busy time, and that a previous campaign built a whole strategy on misreading them -- and the cost table in this campaign's own policy file made the same mistake anyway. The campaign already had a second, independent measurement pointing the same way and did not connect it: L011 recorded that removing 40% of the Newton-Schulz iterations returned only about 0.2% of step time, which is the signature of a GPU that is busy, not one that is waiting. The competing explanation, that mfu_percent is computed against a wrong FLOP count, is weak: the same estimate_flops figure reproduces the recorded MFU to four significant figures and was independently used to catch the parameter-count error in L015.
mitigation: Stop pricing FLOP-adding interventions as free. A capacity arm that raises flops_per_token will cost step count, and at roughly -0.063 bpb per e-fold of steps that cost is first-order, not a rounding error. The ordering this implies is that ZERO-FLOP capacity beats FLOP-buying capacity: raising value-embedding density adds a third more parameters at exactly unchanged flops_per_token, whereas widening the MLP does not. The direct measurement is a gpu_slack_frac observable -- cuda events around the step, read after the charged clock stops -- and until it exists the honest position is that the GPU is substantially busy and every capacity proposal must predict its step-count cost explicitly rather than assert the FLOPs are free.
observation: tools/direction.py has priced the capacity family as 'GPU-only, near-free (GPU idle ~90% of the run)' and the attention, ve_placement and attention_detail families as 'GPU-only, near-free'. Every valid control reports mfu_percent 42.2 to 42.7. MFU is achieved model FLOPs over peak across the WHOLE step, so 42.62% of an H200's 989.5 TF bf16 peak is 421.7 TF/s sustained, or 125.4 TFLOP inside a 297.3 ms step. For the GPU to be idle 90% of the step it would have to sustain 426% of peak while active, which is impossible; even at a generous 60% of peak while active the GPU is busy about 71% of the step.

applies_when: runs are placed on more than one physical GPU of this host, which is every wave wider than one
diagnosis: The devices are not equally fast, and the whole effect L006 named a slot bias is device speed. The core-block story was an artifact of the dispatcher assigning cores BY SLOT while also assigning GPUs by slot, so the two moved together in every wave until the Q1a quad wave crossed them -- and the campaign ran that crossing without noticing it was the experiment L006 said was needed. L017's further claim, that the offset grows with our own concurrency, is refuted by the same data: gpu4 averages 980.0 steps at width 2 and 980.0 at width 4, gpu6 1010.8 and 1010.0, gpu7 1019.6 and 1020.0. Q1a's apparent monotone-in-slot spread was simply slots 0-3 landing on gpu4,5,6,7 in speed order. The honest reading is that L006 measured a real and important effect and mis-attributed its cause; L013 built a correct counterbalancing discipline on the wrong variable; and L017 inferred a width effect from a confound.
mitigation: Counterbalance on GPU, not on core block, and at any width -- there is no width penalty, so the full four-GPU allocation is usable and the earlier advice to idle half the fleet was wrong and is withdrawn. A treatment must occupy each GPU of its wave equally often across the waves of a comparison. The residual noise is smaller than the campaign has been quoting: within-GPU control sd is 0.000085-0.000105, so a GPU-counterbalanced two-wave design resolves roughly 0.00013, not 0.000183. Everything measured so far survives: the ns=3 verdict swapped its treatment across gpu6 and gpu7 and is therefore GPU-counterbalanced by accident, and wd_const's +0.009 is an order above any device offset.
observation: Crosstabbing GPU against taskset core block across all 36 valid 2-epoch runs settles what L006 assumed. Holding the GPU fixed and changing the core block moves nothing: gpu6 runs 1010-1013 steps on cores 96-107 and 1010 on cores 120-131; gpu7 runs 1018-1022 on 108-119 and 1020 on 132-143; gpu4 runs 980 on 96-107 and 977-983 on 120-131. Holding the core block fixed and changing the GPU moves ~30 steps: cores 96-107 give 1010-1013 on gpu6 but 980 on gpu4; cores 108-119 give 1018-1022 on gpu7 but 999 on gpu5. Per-GPU control means are gpu4 0.993558 at 980 steps, gpu5 0.992409 at 999, gpu6 0.991600 at 1010.5, gpu7 0.991111 at 1019.4 -- a spread of 0.002447, against 0.002710 predicted by the step law from the step counts alone. Within a single GPU the control sd is 0.000085 (gpu6, n=11) and 0.000105 (gpu7, n=14).

applies_when: never; this record exists to mark the retraction
diagnosis: There is no width effect. The four-wide spread was the four GPUs' intrinsic speed difference, which the two-wide waves never exposed because they always used the same two devices. This lesson reached the wrong conclusion because it treated slot index as the variable when slot index determined BOTH core block and GPU. It is retracted rather than merely superseded, because its prescription -- prefer two-wide waves and accept two idle GPUs -- actively cost throughput for no measurement benefit.
mitigation: Use the full four-GPU allocation. See L020_the_offset_is_the_gpu_not_the_core_block for the correct model.
observation: L017 claimed the per-slot penalty grows with the number of our own concurrent trainers, citing a four-wide control wave that spread 0.002342 across slots against 0.00047 for a two-wide pair. Holding the GPU fixed, mean step counts are: gpu4 980.0 at width 2 and 980.0 at width 4; gpu5 998.0 and 999.0; gpu6 1010.8 and 1010.0; gpu7 1019.6 and 1020.0.

applies_when: Muon with a NorMuon-style second-moment rescale is in use at this scale; the effect is contested by one transfer-3 claim measured at roughly 9x our batch which reports the after-Newton-Schulz ordering as better
diagnosis: The mechanism is what the three source papers described: reshaping the row scale of the momentum BEFORE orthogonalization changes which singular directions the polar iteration equalizes, and at this operating point that is worth about a thousandth of a bpb. The result required three separate corrections to become visible, and each is worth recording because each would have buried it. The first implementation did not engage at all -- 99.8% of the buffer clamped -- and its three runs read as a small null. The analysis then pooled those non-engaged runs with the repaired ones under a shared label and reported no effect. And the earlier design counterbalanced on taskset core block, which carries no signal, rather than on the physical GPU, which carries about 0.0024. One honest caveat remains on attribution rather than on adoption: this arm removes output-side NorMuon adaptivity and adds input-side equilibration in the same edit, so it is two aligned factors and the win cannot be assigned to the addition alone.
mitigation: Adopt precond='pre' as the new platform candidate, but confirm it first: a single quad-counterbalanced pair of waves is n=4 pairings, and the four deltas span +0.000301 to -0.002348, so the mean is well clear of the resolution while the spread is wide. Re-run the comparison once more before folding it into the control, and when doing so put the two factors on separate arms -- remove-post-only against add-pre-only -- so the attribution question is answered rather than left open.
observation: Moving the NorMuon second-moment rescale ahead of the Newton-Schulz polar iteration, with the momentum rescaled to unit RMS per matrix first, lowered val_bpb by a quad-counterbalanced mean of -0.001147 against a GPU-counterbalanced resolution of 0.000265 -- 4.3x the resolution. The four within-pair deltas were +0.000301 (treatment on gpu4), -0.001719 (gpu7), -0.002348 (gpu5) and -0.000821 (gpu6); the treatment occupied every one of the four devices exactly once, so the device profile cancels by construction. secmom_clamp_frac was 0.0 and secmom_ortho_ratio 15.08 on all four treatment arms, against 0.486 on every control, so the activation predicate of hyp_precond_pre_r1_v3 is satisfied. Mean step_ms_med was 304.47 for the treatment and 304.86 for the controls, a throughput difference of -0.13%. The best single val_bpb of the campaign is now 0.990345, held by precond_rms_A_s3_treat.

applies_when: the gate can freeze new decisions while a wave-atomicity guard sizes waves from the full queue
diagnosis: Two independently correct rules deadlocked. The decision cutoff removes non-control entries created after a council artifact went stale, so prose cannot authorise new science; that left each wave holding only its control. The wave-atomicity guard then compared the runnable members against the number the wave was QUEUED with, saw a shortfall, concluded the wave had been split, and refused the remnant -- including the control, which the cutoff had deliberately left runnable because controls are the instrument and are exempt. The interaction defeats an explicit design goal stated in the gate's own output: already-queued work keeps launching and GPUs do not idle for prose. Neither rule is wrong; the split guard was simply counting a temporarily frozen member as a permanent casualty.
mitigation: wave_sizes() now takes the decision cutoff and excludes members frozen by it from the denominator, so a wave whose treatment is temporarily frozen is not mistaken for one whose treatment was claimed and lost. The distinction that matters is permanence: a claimed-or-completed member is gone for good and its wave really is split, whereas a cutoff-frozen member returns as soon as a council artifact is refreshed. The real remedy for the freeze itself is to write the overdue round, which is the point of the cadence.
observation: At 2026-08-19T04:39Z the dispatcher began logging WAVE SPLIT for every queued wave -- zloss01_A and zloss01_B at 2 of 4 members runnable, VE_A and VE_B at 1 of 2 -- and refused to launch any of them, leaving four free GPUs idle. None of those runs had ever started. The gate at that moment reported both council artifacts stale (round 106 min old, critique 95 min, against a 90 min cadence) and therefore NEW DECISIONS FROZEN.

applies_when: the gate can freeze part of a wave while the rest remains runnable
diagnosis: Excluding frozen members made the wave look complete when it was merely not-yet-runnable, and a wave that launches half of itself is worse than one that waits. The control would have run now and its treatment minutes or hours later in a different wave, on a different device, under different host load -- which is exactly the cross-wave drift the wave_group mechanism was built to eliminate. The first fix cured the deadlock and reintroduced the disease it was protecting against, in a subtler form: instead of refusing to launch, it launched something useless. The distinction that was missing is between a member that is GONE (claimed or completed -- the wave really is split) and one that is merely WAITING (frozen by the cutoff -- the wave is intact but not ready).
mitigation: next_batch() now computes wave sizes twice -- once excluding frozen members and once including them -- and HOLDS any wave where the two disagree, logging WAVE HELD with the count. A split wave is still refused, a frozen wave now waits, and only a genuinely complete wave launches. tests/test_wave_launch.py case 5c asserts that a lone runnable control does not go out and that the pair launches together once the freeze lifts. The four control runs already spent are not wasted -- they are valid controls and enrich the corpus that sets the resolution -- but they bought no comparison.
observation: The first fix for the freeze/split deadlock (L022) excluded cutoff-frozen members from the wave-size denominator so a wave with a frozen treatment would not be mistaken for a split one. The dispatcher then launched that wave's CONTROLS alone: zloss01_A_s1_ctrl, zloss01_A_s2_ctrl, zloss01_B_s0_ctrl and zloss01_B_s3_ctrl went out at 04:45 on all four GPUs while both zloss treatments stayed frozen.

applies_when: a quad-counterbalanced design pairs treatment against control within a wave rather than within a device
diagnosis: The effect is real and better supported than was claimed, but the stated basis for the claim was unsound. '4.3x the resolution' compared a mean against a constant borrowed from the CONTROL corpus while the deltas actually in hand scattered 4.4x wider than that constant -- the same error the campaign had already criticised in its own verdict tool, where a fixed literal stood in for the residual of the data. The cause of the excess scatter is that a same-wave pair is a CROSS-GPU pair, so the entire device profile sits inside each delta; gpu4 and gpu7 differ by about 0.0025, which is larger than the effect being measured. Counterbalancing removes that term from the MEAN but leaves it in the VARIANCE, which is exactly the wrong place for it when the variance is what licenses the claim. Separately, secmom_ortho_ratio was cited as engagement evidence and is bit-identical at 15.08494568 across all four treatment runs on four different devices: it is a constant of the code path, a flag rather than a measurement. secmom_max, which varies 20.27 to 21.85, is the observable that actually evidences per-run engagement.
mitigation: tools/verdict.py now re-pairs same-GPU across the two waves of a quad design before averaging, and prints the sd, SEM and t of the paired deltas rather than only comparing a mean to a stored resolution. Quote precond as -0.001147 with t = -12.3 on four same-GPU pairings, or -0.001043 after step-law residualization; do NOT quote '4.3x resolution' from the cross-GPU pairing. Do not headline the single best val_bpb of 0.990345: it is a treatment run on gpu7, the fastest device, whose plain control already reaches 0.990908, so that number conflates a device advantage with the mechanism. And do not cite secmom_ortho_ratio as engagement -- replace it in the activation predicate with secmom_max or another quantity that varies run to run. All eight runs used seed 42, so this is still n=1 in seed space.
observation: The precond result was reported as a counterbalanced mean of -0.001147 at '4.3x the resolution of 0.000265'. Two independent audits recomputed it. The four deltas as they were paired -- treatment against the control in the SAME WAVE, which is a different GPU -- are +0.000301, -0.001719, -0.002348, -0.000821: sd 0.001151, SEM 0.000575, t = -1.99. On its own dispersion that mean does not clear two standard errors. Re-pairing the identical eight runs SAME-GPU across the two waves gives -0.000902, -0.001145, -0.001186, -0.001354: the same mean -0.001147, sd 0.000187, SEM 0.000093, t = -12.29, all four negative. Applying the campaign's step law as a control variate to the original pairing gives residuals with mean -0.001043, sd 0.000146, t = -14.25.

applies_when: single-run val_bpb comparisons are used for any policy decision while the device spread exceeds the noise band
diagnosis: The improvement test compared single runs across devices while the devices differ by about 0.0025 (L020_the_offset_is_the_gpu_not_the_core_block), which is nearly four times the band. A single run's val_bpb therefore says more about which GPU it landed on than about the intervention, and a treatment can only register as an improvement by beating the luckiest control on the fastest device -- a bar that has nothing to do with the effect size. The campaign had already built the correct instrument for this (counterbalanced same-GPU pairing) and used it to declare the win, then let a policy that predates that instrument rule the direction stale. The competing reading, that the policy was right and the win is too small to matter, does not survive the arithmetic: -0.001147 at t = -12.3 is 4.3 times the resolution and the raw-best comparison simply cannot see it.
mitigation: family_runs now also credits a family when a COUNTERBALANCED comparison inside it beats the resolution: agenda._counterbalanced_wins pairs each treatment cfg against controls on the SAME device, requires at least two devices, and requires the mean to clear the measured resolution. This does not weaken rotation -- tests/test_rotation.py still proves DRY, STALE and the HARD CAP all fire, and the hard cap in particular is unconditional and untouched. Raw val_bpb remains the verdict; what changed is that the comparison is device-to-device rather than between whichever two runs landed on the luckiest hardware. Note the risk this carries: a criterion that keeps a direction alive is exactly the kind of change that should be viewed sceptically, which is why it demands two devices and a resolution-clearing mean rather than any improvement at all.
observation: After precond was confirmed at a same-GPU paired mean of -0.001147 with t = -12.3, tools/agenda.py reported optimizer_geometry with since_improve 7, dry 7 and the exit trigger 'STALE: 7 runs since the last measurable gain - exploited enough'. The policy was about to rotate away from the only direction in the campaign that has produced a win. The cause is that family_runs judged improvement by comparing each run's raw val_bpb against the running best: the previous best was 0.990908, a plain CONTROL that happened to run on gpu7, and the best precond run reached 0.990345 -- an improvement of 0.000563, which is below the 0.00066 band.

applies_when: a queue entry is built by enumerating fields rather than by carrying the validated record forward
diagnosis: A validator and a serializer disagreed about which fields matter, and the validator ran first, so the gate reported success one line before the value was discarded. This is the same shape as L009, where the queue sync validated locally and shipped a stale entry, and the same shape as the observable defects in L014 and L016: a check that passes on a value the system then fails to carry. The failure is invisible by construction, because the only symptom is a downstream check quietly deciding it has nothing to do -- there is no error, no warning, and the round looks correctly queued.
mitigation: queue_from_round.py now copies hypothesis_id onto the persisted entry, and the 16 round-2 entries were repaired in place before any of them launched. General rule for this campaign, now stated twice over: after a validator accepts a field, read that field back from the artifact the executor will actually consume -- the local queue for a door check, the HOST queue for a launch (L009), the result record for an activation check. A check is only worth what survives to the thing being checked.
observation: All 16 round-2 entries were queued with no hypothesis_id field. tools/queue_from_round.py validates e['hypothesis_id'] on the ROUND's queue block and refuses any treatment lacking it -- that check passed -- but the persisted queue entry was constructed from an explicit field list that omitted the key. coe.py E3 and E4 and tools/verdict.py all begin with `hid = q.get('hypothesis_id'); if not hid: continue`, so every one of those runs would have executed attached to nothing and the activation machinery would have silently disengaged.

applies_when: several tensors share a leading dimension and a diagnostic selects among them by shape
diagnosis: A shape filter was used as an identity test on tensors that share a shape by construction. The composition problem is the worse half: a diagnostic whose definition depends on the treatment cannot support a cross-arm comparison at all, and it would have produced a confidently wrong number rather than an obviously missing one. This is the third instance of the same class today, after `_wide[0]` selecting the ve_gate and the treatment-only prints of L016 -- an observable is an experiment and needs the same scepticism as a result.
mitigation: Selection is now by parameter-group POSITION, which is fixed by setup_optimizer, rather than by shape. ve_emb_rms_final reduces over ALL value-embedding tables so the number means the same thing whether there are four or eight, and a companion ve_table_count is emitted so the composition is visible rather than assumed. The 16 queued round-2 variants were rebuilt against the corrected telemetry and their queue entries updated in place before any launched.
observation: The shared telemetry selected embedding tensors with `p.shape[0] == vocab_size`. lm_head.weight, wte.weight and every value-embedding table all satisfy that and all sit in AdamW groups, which are built in the order lm_head, wte, value_embeds, resid, x0 (baseline/train.py:258-262). So `ve_emb_rms_final`, the one diagnostic meant to show the new value-embedding capacity being used, took the first match and printed the LM HEAD's RMS. `head_moment_fill` averaged exp_avg over the head, wte and every VE table together -- and because ve:1 ADDS four tables, that statistic changes its own composition with the treatment, so the treatment and control arms would not have been measuring the same quantity.

applies_when: a mechanism family is registered under a name absent from lit.ALL_FAMILIES, or every run shares one seed
diagnosis: The family was invented when precond was registered as a mechanism, and it was given a name the rotation controller does not know. The anti-monoculture backstop -- the one trigger the campaign's design calls unconditional -- therefore could not fire on the direction that had consumed most of the budget, and by the letter no trigger had tripped. The seed uniformity is a separate and larger hole: the reported band and every resolution figure are fixed-seed quantities containing zero seed variance, so a t of -12.3 describes the precision of a delta at one initialisation and one data order. precond is not a model-preserving change, so pairing gives no protection against a seed effect. The campaign has been quoting precision where it has no estimate of reproducibility.
mitigation: precond is re-homed into optimizer_numeric, which the ledger knows; that family now honestly shows 9 runs against the hard cap of 12, and its claims and lessons already lived there. A mechanism family must use a name in lit.ALL_FAMILIES or it is invisible to rotation. On seeds: eight stacked runs at seed 42 were dropped from the queue and replaced with a GPU-counterbalanced repeat of the precond comparison at SEED 43, which answers the reproducibility question and doubles as the replication L021's mitigation already demanded. Until that lands, quote precond as a single-seed result. Also removed: direction.py was printing the superseded slot-order counterbalancing prescription beside the L020 device model, giving a reader two contradictory rules and two resolutions both looking current.
observation: tools/agenda.py reported optimizer_numeric with runs=2 while the direction had been active for the entire campaign and seven precond runs had executed. Those seven were attributed to a mechanism family named optimizer_geometry, which is a key in direction.MECHANISM_FAMILIES but NOT in lit.ALL_FAMILIES -- and agenda.candidates iterates lit.ALL_FAMILIES, so the family never appeared in the twelve-row ledger and its runs were counted by nothing. DRY, STALE and the unconditional HARD CAP were all computed against a number that omitted the campaign's dominant program. Separately, every one of the 54 valid runs used seed 42.

applies_when: the instrument estimators return a value. If a change to the harness, the host, or the operating point invalidates them, noise_band() returns None, the refusal lifts on its own, and recalibration is allowed again without an override.
diagnosis: Standalone control blocks were queued through tools/queue_controls.py, which had a DEFAULT rationale string still describing the very first calibration problem ('the four existing controls ran back-to-back on one GPU'). Because the justification was a default rather than an argument, no caller ever had to ask whether it was still true, and it stopped being true after the first two waves. A yoked control queued ALONGSIDE its treatment is a different thing entirely and was never the problem: that control is load-bearing, is charged against the treatment it serves, and stays at 1:1 by construction.
mitigation: queue_controls.py now requires --measures naming the instrument quantity, and _already_measured() refuses outright when noise_band / device_resolution / slot_bias already return an estimate, printing the current control:treatment ratio in the refusal. Override needs --force with a stated reason. Yoked controls are unaffected -- they are queued by queue_quad.py and queue_from_round.py, which this lesson does not touch.
observation: 43 of the first 54 valid runs were CONTROLS and 11 were treatments, a 3.91:1 ratio, recomputed from runs/sweep/results/*.json by is_platform(). The three quantities that budget bought -- within-wave band 0.000661, slot offset +0.000467, per-GPU resolution 0.000271 -- were all estimated well before the last of those control waves ran, so the marginal waves bought precision on numbers that were already precise enough to resolve every effect being chased.

applies_when: any hypothesis declares an activation diagnostic. Retire this only if E3 is extended to compare the diagnostic across arms automatically, at which point the check outlives the lesson.
diagnosis: Two distinct errors wearing one coat. A NON-DISCRIMINATING diagnostic -- a number the control produces too -- proves nothing about engagement, though it can still rule out a failure mode, which is what clamp_frac legitimately does. A CONSTANT diagnostic is worse: identical bits across independent runs mean the quantity is fixed by the code path, so no run could ever have failed the test. Neither error is visible from the hypothesis record alone; both require reading the emitted numbers of BOTH arms, which is why E3 checking only that the field exists was not enough.
mitigation: hyp_precond_pre_r1_v4 replaces the diagnostic with secmom_max > 1.0, which measures 20.27-21.85 in treatments against 0.247-0.286 in controls and varies within each arm. The general rule this campaign should apply when declaring any activation observable: name a quantity whose value in the CONTROL is known and different, and confirm it is not bit-identical across runs. A diagnostic that cannot separate the arms is not a diagnostic.
observation: hyp_precond_pre_r1_v3 declared secmom_clamp_frac < 0.01 as its activation rule. Recomputed from the records, that field is 0.0 in all four treatments AND 0.0 in all four wave-mate controls and in zloss01_A_s1_ctrl. Its written predicate also required secmom_ortho_ratio far below 1, while the shipped edit pins that value at 15.08494568 -- above 1, and bit-identical across precond_rms_A_s0_treat, precond_rms_A_s3_treat, precond_rms_B_s1_treat and precond_rms_B_s2_treat, so it is a path constant rather than a measurement.

applies_when: always, as an accounting rule: a stranded treatment is charged as a lost experiment, not as a lost run. Retire only if wave membership becomes immutable at queue time, which would make the stranding impossible rather than merely visible.
diagnosis: Downstream consequence of L023: a wave launched its controls without their treatments, which was recorded at the time as wasted control runs. The larger cost was not visible until now -- the treatments became UNRUNNABLE, because a wave is sized from the queue and a member whose wave-mates have finished can no longer share their host conditions. Running it later would be a cross-wave comparison wearing a wave_group label, which is precisely the confound the grouping exists to prevent. So the loss is not 4 controls; it is 4 controls plus an entire experiment that was queued, survived the door, and never produced a single datum.
mitigation: Two changes already shipped and proven by tests. host/dispatch.py holds a wave whose members are frozen rather than launching the runnable remainder (tests/test_wave_launch.py case 5c), and permanently split waves are now tombstoned as INVALID results rather than refused forever (case 5d), so this loss appears in tools/analyze.py instead of sitting in the queue looking like pending work. The z-loss question itself is NOT closed by this: it was never measured. If it is wanted, re-queue it as a fresh counterbalanced quad through tools/queue_quad.py with a registered hypothesis -- which the original entries lacked, carrying hypothesis_id null.
observation: zloss01_A_s0_treat, zloss01_A_s3_treat, zloss01_B_s1_treat and zloss01_B_s2_treat were retired unrun by the dispatcher's split-wave tombstone. Their four wave-mate controls (zloss01_A_s1_ctrl, zloss01_A_s2_ctrl, zloss01_B_s0_ctrl, zloss01_B_s3_ctrl) had already completed at val_bpb 0.993659, 0.992781, 0.992003 and 0.991567, so the pairings could never be reformed. The zloss=0.1 arm therefore has FOUR controls and ZERO treatments, and no verdict about z-loss exists or can be constructed from these records.

applies_when: the Muon weight-decay schedule is the one in baseline/train.py and the budget is 300 charged seconds at about 1000 steps. A change to the schedule or a materially different step count would reopen the question.
diagnosis: The pair was NOT GPU-counterbalanced: the treatment sat on gpu6 and gpu5 while its controls sat on gpu7 and gpu4, so a fixed device offset is formally inseparable from the effect. That does not rescue the arm. Every delta is more than 3x the largest slot offset ever measured on this box (0.002645) and both share a sign, so the SIGN is safe even though the magnitude is not pinned. +0.009 is roughly 34x the 0.000271 resolution; no device offset on this host is remotely that large. What remains genuinely uncertain is only whether the true harm is 0.008 or 0.010.
mitigation: blocks_values forbids wd_const at or above 0.4. The axis is not closed below that: the scheduled default and smaller constant values were never tested and remain legitimate experiments, which is exactly why this uses the VALUE-level hook rather than blocks_keys -- forbidding the wd_const KEY would retire an axis on the evidence of a single bad value, the error L007_ns_above_five_is_a_noop_v2 already documents. If the magnitude is ever wanted precisely, it needs a same-GPU swapped quad through tools/queue_quad.py, not another unpaired repeat.
observation: Holding Muon weight decay constant at 0.40 instead of following its schedule cost +0.010441 on gpu6 (wd040_slot0 1.001430 vs ctrl_R1W_A_slot1 0.990989) and +0.008200 on gpu5 (wd040_slot1 1.002015 vs ctrl_R1W_B_slot0 0.993815), a mean of +0.009321. Step counts moved little (1012 vs 1020, 999 vs 977), so this is not a throughput effect -- the arm simply trained to a worse model at the same budget.

applies_when: any hypothesis argues from a FLOP, memory or time share. Retire when a queue-door check computes the intervention's own delta automatically.
diagnosis: A component's share of cost was substituted for the share the INTERVENTION actually removes. The 26% figure is correct about attention and says nothing about this edit. The error inflated the expected throughput leg by about 3.3x, and it is seductive because the large number is true -- it is simply the answer to a different question. This is the same shape of mistake as L011_ns_reduction_is_a_valid_negative, where an orthogonalization thought to be worth chasing turned out to be ~0.2% of step time; there the correction arrived only after a GPU wave was spent, here it arrived from the literature before launch.
mitigation: hyp_swdiv_short_window_halved_r1_v3 supersedes v2 with the recomputed 7.9% and holds the 0.0006 prediction threshold unchanged rather than lowering it to fit. The general rule: when a hypothesis rests on a cost share, compute the DELTA the edit produces from the frozen source -- estimate_flops is right there and takes seconds -- rather than quoting the enclosing component's total. State it as 'X of Y removed', never as 'this touches the Z% part'.
observation: hyp_swdiv_short_window_halved_r1_v2 justified the swdiv 2->4 arm with 'attention is 62.91M of the 239.08 MFLOP per token, about 26%, so halving the short window is a FLOP change large enough to move step count'. Recomputed from baseline/train.py estimate_flops over the real window list [1024,1024,1024,2048,1024,1024,1024,2048] at sequence_len 2048, the edit takes attention from 62.91M to 44.04M. It removes 18.87M per token, 7.9% of the total -- not 26%. The two long-window layers hold 40% of the attention term and the edit does not touch them.

applies_when: gpu_span_ms is measured as an outer event pair around a region containing host synchronisation or data loading. Retire when per-kernel accumulation or an external profiler replaces it.
diagnosis: A pair of torch.cuda.Event markers measures the ELAPSED TIME between two points on the stream, and that interval INCLUDES any period the GPU sat idle waiting for the CPU to enqueue work. Because ev0 is recorded before the micro-step loop and ev1 after optimizer.step(), the bracket spans the next(train_loader) calls too, so the span is the step by construction and 1 - span/step is forced to zero no matter how idle the device actually was. The instrument therefore cannot answer the question it was built for, and its near-zero reading is NOT evidence that the GPU is saturated. This is the same error CLAUDE.md already warns about for fwdbwd_frac -- mistaking a CPU-side or stream-side wall-clock span for GPU busy time -- reproduced in a new place by the person who had just read the warning.
mitigation: Do not cite gpu_slack_frac or gpu_span_ms_med as evidence about GPU utilisation, and do not let any FLOP-pricing argument rest on them; the mechanism loader_slack_prices_gpu_flops_at_zero_merged remains UNINSTRUMENTED and its activation observable is still unmet. Measuring real busy time needs either the SUM of per-kernel durations rather than an outer span, or a controlled FLOPs comparison -- change the FLOPs and see what happens to step count, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md prescribes and what the swdiv arm is designed to do. The fields are left emitted rather than removed, because they are a correct measurement of the STEP SPAN and the close agreement with step_ms_med is a useful check that the event pair brackets the whole step.
observation: The gpu_slack_frac instrument shipped this session reads 0.000210, 0.000200, 0.000206 and 0.000218 across R2V_A_s0_treat, R2V_A_s1_ctrl, R2V_A_s2_ctrl and R2V_A_s3_treat -- i.e. essentially zero slack on every arm. The reason is visible in the raw fields: gpu_span_ms_med is 317.418 against step_ms_med 317.5, 305.865 against 305.9, 301.713 against 301.8, and 305.331 against 305.4. The span tracks the step time to within a tenth of a millisecond in all four runs.

applies_when: the 300-second budget, ~1000 steps and the fixed dataset whose second epoch ends near 510M tokens. A larger budget or fresh data would change the boundary interaction and must be re-measured.
diagnosis: A 33% larger model that runs slower still wins at a fixed 300 seconds, so the quality gained per step more than repays the throughput lost. This CONTRADICTS the registered literature prior, which is the point worth recording: v3_injection_at_all_layers_worse_than_one_layer, v3_dense_per_layer_stream_expansion_saturates and v3_memory_benefit_is_pathway_not_table_content all pointed the other way. Each was scored transfer 1, 1 and 2 respectively -- image autoregression, 4B-token tokenizer-transfer fine-tuning, and a 2.5B MoE -- and this is what an honest low transfer score is FOR. The claims keep their 'opposes' stance and are not rewritten; what is now known is that they do not carry to 50M parameters at 300 seconds.
mitigation: Treat ve=1 as a confirmed lever at this operating point, NOT as a settled magnitude: it is single-seed (42) and one of the four cells is void. The gpu4 cell (R2V_A_s0_treat) finished at 501.2M tokens and final_epoch 1.0 against its control's 2.0, because the extra parameters cost enough throughput to drop it under the ~510M two-epoch boundary -- so counterbalancing is INCOMPLETE and precisely on the slowest device, where the throughput cost bites hardest. Re-run that cell before quoting the magnitude, and note the boundary interaction is a real hazard for any parameter-adding treatment here.
observation: ve stride 2 -> 1 (a value embedding on EVERY layer, tables 4 -> 8, params 50.3M -> 67.1M) lowered val_bpb by a same-GPU paired mean of -0.001487 over three devices: gpu5 -0.001367 (R2V_B_s1_treat vs R2V_A_s1_ctrl), gpu6 -0.001364 (R2V_B_s2_treat vs R2V_A_s2_ctrl), gpu7 -0.001731 (R2V_A_s3_treat vs R2V_B_s3_ctrl); sd 0.000211, sem 0.000122, t=-12.2 against a resolution of 0.000267. R2V_A_s3_treat at 0.989819 is the lowest val_bpb the campaign has produced. Activation passed on every treatment arm: n_ve_layers 8 against a rule of >4. The treatment completed FEWER steps than its control in every cell (972 vs 992, 984 vs 1005, 993 vs 1012) and won regardless.

applies_when: waves are assigned by sorted-free-GPU rather than pinned to a device set. Retire if the dispatcher gains device pinning for counterbalanced waves.
diagnosis: A quad counterbalances WITHIN a wave, which is why it was preferred over 2-wide pairs. But the A/B layout pair -- [T,C,C,T] then [C,T,T,C] -- only completes the design if BOTH waves land on the SAME four devices. The dispatcher assigns by sorted free GPU, so a device that has not released yet is silently replaced by any other free one, and the swap that was supposed to cancel a device offset instead introduces a new device with no measured offset at all. The operator explicitly judged this hazard 'moot' after reverting from pairs to quads; that was wrong. Reverting removed the CAPACITY route to the hazard and left the DEVICE-SET route wide open, and the second route fired within one experiment.
mitigation: Read the gpu field of every arm before quoting a counterbalanced mean -- tools/verdict.py keys arms by device and will report 'treatment only ever on {X}' rather than averaging across a broken swap, so the failure surfaces as a refusal instead of a confident wrong number. To repair an experiment damaged this way, queue one further wave in the SWAPPED layout and confirm it landed on the same devices; do not assume it did. A stronger fix, not yet built, is for the dispatcher to pin a wave to a named device set and hold rather than substitute -- but that trades throughput for design integrity and should not be adopted without measuring how often it would idle the box.
observation: R2S_A launched on gpu4-7 with the treatment on gpu4 and gpu7. Eight seconds after it finished, R2S_B launched on gpu1, gpu4, gpu5 and gpu6 -- gpu7 had not yet released -- putting the treatment on gpu4 for a SECOND time and never on gpu7. gpu1 then acquired a foreign tenant and was invalidated (rc=1, no val_bpb) and quarantined. Device coverage across the two waves is therefore treatment on gpu4 twice, gpu5 and gpu7 once; control on gpu5, gpu6 twice, gpu1 void. Exactly ONE same-GPU pair survives (gpu5), where a full quad pair would have given four.

applies_when: depth 8, the 300-second budget, and this SSSL architecture. A materially deeper stack would reopen the question, since the published lineage this was drawn from uses far more layers.
diagnosis: A genuine negative, not a non-activation, and the cleanest attribution the campaign has produced. Because the edit adds one elementwise add per lower-half layer and no matmul, it cannot buy or cost steps -- and the step counts confirm it did not -- so the entire effect is quality, with none of the throughput entanglement that has explained most of this campaign's variance. That is why the spread across four independent devices is only 0.00015. At this depth (8 layers) and this budget, routing lower-half activations into the upper half actively hurts; the lambdas grew to ~0.2, so the model USED the path and was worse for it, rather than learning to ignore it.
mitigation: blocks_values forbids unet at or above 1, which is its only enabled setting, so the mechanism cannot be re-queued while this lesson holds. Note for proposal review: `unet` was the INDEPENDENT top pick of both the explorer and the pragmatist in round 3, and their agreement carried no evidential weight whatever -- convergence among proposers is not evidence, and this is the cheapest available reminder of that.
observation: Zero-initialised U-net skip connections from the lower half of the stack to the upper half RAISED val_bpb by a same-GPU paired mean of +0.004123 over all four devices: gpu4 +0.004195, gpu5 +0.004042, gpu6 +0.004184, gpu7 +0.004070. sd 0.000078, sem 0.000039, t=105.6 against a resolution of 0.000297 -- about 14x. The mechanism ENGAGED: skip_lambda_absmean reached 0.205189, 0.198856, 0.200111 and 0.203682 on the four treatment arms from an initialisation of exactly zero. Step counts moved -19, +5, +14 and -12 against their controls, i.e. no consistent direction.

applies_when: make_variant.build generates a mechanism that adds an nn.Parameter. Retire when the assert is repaired or replaced by a per-parameter group-membership check.
diagnosis: The guard exists to catch precisely the failure mode a new mechanism introduces -- a freshly added Parameter that never reaches an optimizer group, and so silently never trains. Deleting it instead of updating its arithmetic removes the check at the exact moment it becomes relevant.
