This run got the grouping right, so nothing was lost here; the cost is that the NEXT mechanism to add a parameter has no guard, and its failure would look like a null result rather than a bug. Found by an independent audit reading the generated source, not the cfg -- which is the whole reason E4 insists on reading the source.
mitigation: make_variant should UPDATE the assert's expected count when it adds a parameter group, or replace it with a structural check that every nn.Parameter appears in exactly one optimizer group -- the latter is stronger and does not need arithmetic maintenance. Until that is built, any mechanism variant that introduces a Parameter must be diffed against the control and its telemetry checked for a non-zero learned value, which is what caught this: skip_lambda_absmean reached ~0.2 from a zero init, proving the parameter did train.
observation: Diffing the unet variant dffe9e3019ae.py against the control 82bc169727c0.py shows an edit nobody declared: the assert comparing len(list(self.parameters())) against the sum of the optimizer group lengths is DELETED rather than updated. The declared edits -- the skip_lambdas parameter, its addition to x0_params, the forward-pass skips and the telemetry -- are all present and correct, and skip_lambdas IS properly grouped, so the +0.004123 unet result (L037_unet_skips_are_a_clean_valid_negative) is numerically unaffected: an assert changes no math.

applies_when: QK-norm is in the architecture, which pins query and key RMS to 1.0 and makes any diagnostic derived from it constant across arms.
diagnosis: QK-norm normalises queries and keys to unit RMS by construction, so qk_q_rms_final could never have been anything but 1.0 in either arm. The diagnostic was chosen for sounding related to the intervention rather than for separating the arms. The hypothesis hyp_qk_suppress_r3 named this exact case in its own falsifier -- 'qk_q_rms_final and qk_k_rms_final land inside the control range -- suppression did not bind, INCONCLUSIVE' -- so the pre-registered reading applies and the +0.001226 is NOT attributable to the mechanism. It is real and reproducible; what is unknown is whether the learning-rate suppression bound at all, or whether something else moved. Non-activation is inconclusive, never a negative, or good ideas are retired for free.
mitigation: Do NOT block qk_suppress: the axis is untested, not refuted. To retest, declare a diagnostic that separates the arms -- the suppressed layers' Q/K weight RMS or the realised LR multiplier, neither of which QK-norm pins. Mechanically enforced now: claims.diagnostic_would_discriminate() checks a proposed diagnostic against the CONTROL corpus before a hypothesis is registered and refuses one every control also satisfies. This is the THIRD instance of L030 in one session (secmom_clamp_frac, num_steps>0, qk_q_rms_final), all registered after that lesson existed, which is the evidence that prose alone does not prevent recurrence.
observation: qk_suppress=0.1 raised val_bpb by a fully counterbalanced same-GPU paired mean of +0.001226 over four devices (deltas 0.001234, 0.001048, 0.001424, 0.001197; sd 0.000155, sem 0.000077, t=15.8 against a resolution of 0.000289). Read on val_bpb alone that is a clean 4.2x negative. But the declared activation diagnostic qk_q_rms_final reads exactly 1.0 in all four treatments AND in all 25 controls that emit it, so it cannot show the mechanism engaged.

applies_when: the 300-second budget with the frozen packing loop and roughly 1000 steps at 524288 tokens per step. A budget large enough to change the update count materially would reopen it.
diagnosis: At a fixed 300-second budget the model is far ABOVE its critical batch size, so halving the number of optimizer updates costs vastly more than the gradient-noise reduction returns. The hypothesis deliberately predicted EITHER direction because the registered mechanism concerns which side of the critical batch size this point sits on; the answer is unambiguous. Note the step law may NOT be used to explain this away: it was fitted at 524288 tokens per step and this arm moves that very quantity, so applying it across the change would violate the fit's own operating point. Raw val_bpb at 300 seconds is the verdict and it is decisive.
mitigation: blocks_values forbids tbs at or above 20. The DOWNWARD direction is untested and stays open -- if the model is above its critical batch size, a SMALLER tokens-per-step may pay, and that is now the interesting arm on this axis rather than a further increase.
observation: tbs 19 -> 20, doubling tokens per step from 524288 to 1048576, RAISED val_bpb by a fully counterbalanced same-GPU paired mean of +0.022545 over four devices (deltas 0.022955, 0.022588, 0.022468, 0.022168; sd 0.000326, sem 0.000163, t=138.5 against a resolution of 0.000287) -- about 78x the resolution and by far the largest effect the campaign has measured. Step counts roughly halved as expected: 492 vs 992, 512 vs 1005, 502 vs 972, 509 vs 1011. Activation confirmed: tokens_per_step reads 1048576 in every treatment against the control's 524288. All arms reached final_epoch 2.0 at comparable total tokens (515.9M vs 520.1M, 536.9M vs 526.9M), so this is a real effect and not an operating-point artefact.

applies_when: sequence length 2048 with the SSSL pattern and the 300-second budget. The long-window layers are untouched and carry 40% of the attention term; a pattern change would need remeasuring.
diagnosis: The mediator behaved exactly as local_span_buys_steps describes: removing 18.874 of 239.078 MFLOP per token (7.9%) bought roughly 3-5% more optimizer steps inside the fixed 300 seconds, and the shorter local context cost little enough quality that the trade paid several times over. This is the opposite outcome to ns=3, where a compute reduction worth ~0.2% of step time bought no steps at all and the arm came back worse -- the difference is that 7.9% is large enough to move the critical path and 0.2% is not.
mitigation: Do NOT block this axis; it is a WIN and the sweep continues. swdiv=8 is queued as rung 2 and is judged rung-to-rung against swdiv=4, not against control, because a knob that pays does so sharply and then flattens. Two process notes worth carrying: the arm needed THREE attempts to measure because a device-set shift broke counterbalancing twice (L036), and its original justification quoted 26% of FLOPs when the edit removes 7.9% (L033) -- the corrected, harder prediction was met anyway, and the 0.0006 threshold was deliberately not lowered after the error was found.
observation: swdiv 2 -> 4, halving the SSSL short-attention span from 1024 to 512, LOWERED val_bpb by a fully counterbalanced same-GPU paired mean of -0.002463 over four devices (deltas -0.002324, -0.002500, -0.002788, -0.002240; sd 0.000242, sem 0.000121, t=-20.3 against a resolution of 0.000284) -- 8.7x the resolution and the largest confirmed effect in the campaign, about 1.7x the ve win and 2.1x precond. Step counts rose in every cell (1010 vs 990, 1029 vs 975, 1043 vs 1013, 1049 vs 999). All arms reached final_epoch 2.0. Activation clean: flops_per_token_M 220.204 against the control's 239.078.

applies_when: the 300-second budget, sequence length 2048, SSSL pattern, and the fixed dataset whose second epoch ends near 510M tokens. The near-cancellation of the throughput terms is specific to these two levers at these values.
diagnosis: The naive sum of the three separately confirmed effects is -0.005097 (-0.002463 swdiv, -0.001487 ve, -0.001147 precond), so the stack realises 86.5% of additive with a shortfall of 0.000689 -- about 2.4x the resolution and therefore RESOLVABLE, not noise. The levers are partly redundant and overwhelmingly complementary. The overlap channel is visible in the step counts and was predicted before the run: ve costs throughput (16.8M added parameters; alone it managed 956 steps on gpu4 and voided at final_epoch 1.0) while swdiv buys it (+3-5%). Stacked, gpu4 ran 991 steps against its control's 992 -- the two nearly cancel in the throughput channel, and that cancellation is where the missing 0.0007 went. Critically, the epoch gate was checked BEFORE val_bpb, so the shortfall cannot be an epoch-boundary artefact of the kind that voided the ve-alone cell; the two explanations are indistinguishable after the fact, which is why the order was fixed in advance.
mitigation: This is a MEASUREMENT, not an adoption. The control remains the unchanged platform, so the 39-run control corpus and per-GPU device model that the 0.000282 resolution rests on stay valid. Adoption would shift every future control by about -0.0044 and retire that instrument; it should follow a second seed, which is not queued because the operator directed single-seed working. State the claim as seed 42 on this host, not as a general result.
observation: precond=pre + ve=1 + swdiv=4 together LOWERED val_bpb by a fully counterbalanced same-GPU paired mean of -0.004408 over four devices (deltas -0.004450, -0.004316, -0.004262, -0.004602; sd 0.000152, sem 0.000076, t=-58.0 against a resolution of 0.000282) -- 15.6x the resolution. All eight arms reached final_epoch 2.0. All three components engaged in the same records: n_ve_layers 8, flops_per_token_M 220.207, secmom_max 17.31 against a control near 0.25. R4X_A_s3_treat at 0.986956 is the campaign's best val_bpb.

applies_when: any gate is added to a decision AFTER the criteria were set. Retire when adoption has happened and the recalibration block has re-measured the resolution.
diagnosis: A gate that cannot be satisfied is not caution, it is a refusal wearing caution's clothing, and it is worse than an explicit refusal because it looks like a pending decision and so is never revisited. The stated reason -- that adoption retires the 70-run control corpus and per-device model the 0.000279 resolution rests on -- is a real cost, but it is a ONE-OFF recalibration cost, whereas measuring every future experiment against a stale baseline is a recurring one. The asymmetry was not weighed; the conservative-sounding option was simply preferred.
mitigation: The seed gate is withdrawn. Adoption proceeds at the next CLEAN BOUNDARY rather than mid-queue, because direction.PLATFORM defines 'control' for is_platform, the device model, the resolution and the queue doors, and the 16 in-flight entries are already paired with old-baseline controls and internally consistent. Sequence: let the swdiv sweep and tbs=18 finish, then change PLATFORM, then run ONE recalibration control block -- which L029 permits precisely because a regime change invalidates the estimators, the documented condition under which its refusal lifts. The claim stays seed-42-on-this-host; adoption does not upgrade the evidence, it only stops paying the stale baseline tax.
observation: The three-lever stack was confirmed at -0.004408 (t=-58.0, four devices, all arms final_epoch 2.0) and satisfied both adoption gates the round council set. Adoption was nonetheless deferred on a THIRD condition added afterwards -- a second-seed replication -- which the operator's standing single-seed directive makes impossible to satisfy. An independent process audit named this a pocket veto and priced it: 16 queued runs are being measured against a control 0.004408 worse than the configuration already demonstrated.

applies_when: sequence length 2048, SSSL pattern, 300-second budget.
diagnosis: The sweep has NOT saturated. The marginal is roughly halving per rung (-0.002298 then -0.001062), which is the saturating shape but has not yet crossed the floor. Judging rung-to-rung rather than against control is what makes this decidable: against control swdiv=8 still looks like a large win and always will, so a control comparison would keep the sweep running long after the marginal gain died.
mitigation: Continue to rung 3, swdiv=16 (short window 128). If the marginal halves again it lands near -0.0005, still above the floor; two more halvings saturate it. Watch the registered floor: the smallest local window any paper in the corpus reports as safe is 50 tokens at 6.5M parameters and sequence 2048, so rung 4 would be entering territory the literature does not support. Note also that swdiv alone at -0.003360 now carries more of the three-lever stack than it did when the stack was measured at swdiv=4; the stack is worth re-measuring once the sweep settles.
observation: swdiv=8 (short window 256) measured -0.003360 against control as a fully counterbalanced same-GPU paired mean over four devices (deltas -0.003165, -0.003264, -0.003636, -0.003375; sd 0.000203, t=-33.1), all arms at final_epoch 2.0, flops_per_token_M 210.767. The clean swdiv=4 quad measured -0.002298, so the RUNG-TO-RUNG marginal is -0.001062, about 3.8x the 0.000279 resolution. Step counts rose again: 1039, 1056, 1071 and 1081 against controls near 990-1010.

applies_when: get_muon_momentum remains step-indexed while the other schedules are progress-indexed. Retire if the ramp is converted to progress-indexing, which would remove the confound at its root but is an edit to schedule semantics and would itself need measuring.
diagnosis: The campaign's largest confirmed result, tbs=18 at -0.007953 (t=-60.7, four devices), is a MIXTURE of two mechanisms: twice as many optimizer updates, and a momentum schedule that reaches full value twice as early in relative terms. No arm run so far can separate them. The raw val_bpb verdict stands -- that configuration really does produce 0.984017 at 300 seconds, and raw val_bpb at 300s is the benchmark -- but the ATTRIBUTION to batch size is not clean, and the hypothesis's stated mechanism (critical batch size) is only part of what the arm changed. Every step-count-moving lever carries a milder version: swdiv=8 shifts the ramp from 30.3% to 27.8%, small but not zero.
mitigation: A mu_warmup knob is added to tools/make_variant.py, editing the 300 in the ramp, and registered as an axis in direction.KNOB_AXES so the policy can see it. The discriminating experiment is tbs=18 with mu_warmup=600, which holds the ramp at the SAME FRACTION of the run as the control: if the gain survives it is batch size, and if it largely vanishes the campaign's biggest win was a schedule effect. Until that runs, tbs=18 must be described as a configuration result and not as evidence about critical batch size.
observation: baseline/train.py:534 defines get_muon_momentum(step) as min(step / 300, 1) -- indexed by STEP -- while get_lr_multiplier and get_weight_decay are indexed by PROGRESS, i.e. elapsed time over budget. Any lever that changes step count therefore changes what FRACTION of training the momentum ramp occupies. Measured on the records: R5T18_A_s1_ctrl runs 991 steps so the ramp completes at 30.3% of the run, while R5T18_A_s3_treat runs 2003 steps and completes it at 15.0%. R4S8_A_s3_treat at 1081 steps sits at 27.8%.

applies_when: any lever changes num_steps materially. swdiv=8 shifts the momentum ramp from 30.3% to 27.8% and carries the same legs in miniature; the effect is small there but not zero.
diagnosis: The queued two-arm decomposition -- mu_warmup=600 holding the ramp fraction, mu_ceil =0.9823 moving the coefficient -- addresses only leg 1. It CANNOT isolate batch size, because at least four other quantities moved simultaneously and two of them (the per-step weight-decay dose and the EMA horizons) plausibly matter as much as the momentum ramp. The -0.007953 result stands as a CONFIGURATION result: that configuration really does reach 0.984017 at 300 seconds, and raw val_bpb at 300s is the benchmark. What is not established, and cannot be established by the currently queued arms, is that the mechanism is critical batch size. The uncharged-warmup leg is worth noting separately because it is the only one whose direction is known: it favours the CONTROL, so the measured win is if anything understated.
mitigation: Do not describe tbs=18 as a batch-size result. R5MU and R5MC still run -- each answers its own question and both are cheap -- but their result must be reported as bounding ONE leg, not as the decomposition. A full attribution needs either a variant that makes every step-indexed quantity progress-indexed (a large edit to schedule semantics, itself needing measurement) or acceptance that at this benchmark 'batch size' and 'schedule shape' are not separable by config alone. The cheapest honest step is the second: state the entanglement and stop claiming the mechanism.
observation: L045 recorded ONE step-indexed quantity moving when tokens-per-step halved: the Muon momentum ramp, min(step/300,1), whose completion shifted from 30.3% of the run to 15.0%. An independent method audit enumerated baseline/train.py and found at least four more, plus one already known. (1) The first 11 steps are UNCHARGED, so the control receives 11 x 524288 = 5.8M free tokens against the tbs=18 arm's 11 x 262144 = 2.9M -- a subsidy that works AGAINST the treatment. (2) Adam bias correction is step-indexed, though it completes by step 50-300. (3) Adam and NorMuon EMA horizons are fixed per STEP, so doubling the step count halves their effective time constant relative to the run. (4) Weight decay is applied per step, so a doubled step count doubles the total decay dose at the same wall clock. (5) grad_accum changed 2 -> 1.

applies_when: a lesson's mitigation introduces a sequencing condition on a decision the lesson was written to unblock. Retire when adoption has occurred and the recalibration block has re-measured resolution at the new platform.
diagnosis: A lesson that fixes a process failure can reintroduce it in its own mitigation, because the mitigation is written while the original failure is salient and the new clause looks like ordinary caution rather than a gate. The specific defect is scope: 'let the swdiv sweep finish' did not distinguish already-launched waves, which are internally consistent and cheap to complete, from unlaunched rungs, which would spend fresh GPU-hours measuring against a baseline the campaign has already agreed is 0.007953 worse. Running R5S16 to satisfy the clause would cost roughly 2.2 GPU-hours to pay exactly the stale-baseline tax that L043 exists to stop paying.
mitigation: L043's sequencing clause is narrowed to: already-LAUNCHED waves finish; UNLAUNCHED rungs do not gate adoption and resume after recalibration at the new platform. Adoption of tbs=18 into direction.PLATFORM is therefore gated on R5MU and R5MC landing, and NOT on R5S16. Adoption is followed by exactly one recalibration control block, which L029 permits because a regime change invalidates the estimators. Falsifier for the adoption itself: if the recalibration wave's within-GPU sd at tbs=18 is not comparable in scale to the current 0.000198, the resolution model breaks and every verdict at the new platform needs a wider band before it is trusted.
observation: L043 was registered to remove a gate that could not be satisfied. Its own mitigation then wrote a new sequencing clause -- 'let the swdiv sweep and tbs=18 finish, then change PLATFORM' -- and by round 6 that clause had become a gate of the same shape. The operator simultaneously HELD tbs=18 adoption on the grounds that R5S16 (swdiv=16) must finish first, and provisionally accepted cutting the 10 non-tbs=18 waves as stale-operating-point, a set that CONTAINS R5S16. An independent synthesizer found the contradiction: the justification for decision 2 and the action of decision 3 cannot both be literally true. Confirmed directly from queue.json -- all 10 cut waves hard-code tbs:19 in their control, 8 of 10 in the treatment as well.

applies_when: any statistic is computed per-factor from runs that may vary more than one factor. Retire when every such estimator is covered by a test asserting a single-factor value against an independent recomputation.
diagnosis: Attribution was written as 'which families does this cfg touch', which is the right question for COVERAGE and the wrong one for EFFECT. A run that moves three keys measures their joint effect; no part of it is evidence about any single key, and L042 had already measured this very stack at 86% of additive, so the campaign held direct evidence the factors were non-additive at the moment it was crediting each with the sum. The consequences differed by instrument and both were live: in selector.py an inflated family effect ranked the queue, and in balance.py an inflated rung decides SATURATION, which decides whether the campaign explores or keeps exploiting a knob. The defect survived because both instruments were read for their conclusions rather than checked against a hand recomputation of a single axis.
mitigation: Only single-factor arms contribute to a single-factor estimate. selector.family_effects now scores a multi-family arm under its own 'stack:a+b' key, so the evidence is kept but cannot masquerade as evidence about a part; balance.sweeps excludes multi-axis runs from the ladders and PRINTS how many it excluded, because a ladder that silently dropped a third of the corpus would read as full coverage. tests/test_guards_fire.py asserts the swdiv=4 rung equals the independently recomputed -0.002194 and fails if a multi-axis arm leaks back in.
observation: Two independent instruments attributed a multi-key arm's FULL device-corrected delta to every factor it touched. tools/selector.py: the three-lever stack R4X_A_s3_treat (ve=1, swdiv=4, precond=pre) contributed -0.004355 to BOTH the attention and ve_placement families, where it stood as each one's largest effect and set the ranking prior for the queue; it also reached a round-6 provenance line labelled 'best swdiv effect across 16 runs'. tools/balance.py: the same arm entered the per-axis ladders, inflating swdiv=4 from -0.002194 to -0.002889 and ve=1 from -0.001432 to -0.002855, and changing the swdiv rung-to-rung marginal by a factor of three. The single-factor arms measure -0.002194 (swdiv 2->4, n=8) and -0.003218 (swdiv 2->8, n=4).

applies_when: the 300-charged-second single-H200 budget with vocab 8192, for any MTP implementation that materialises a second full-width [B,T,V] logits tensor and backprops it. A head that shares or factorises the projection, or a budget long enough that 371 steps is not the binding constraint, is NOT covered and may be proposed again with its own hypothesis.
diagnosis: The extra [B,T,V] backward pass through a vocab-8192 head costs far more time than the denser per-token supervision repays inside a fixed 300-second budget. This is exactly the failure the pre-registered falsifier named, so the arm was well designed: it could have come back either way and the diagnostic separated the readings. Note the campaign's own scoring apparatus had priced this risk with the wrong constant -- a peak_vram clause derived from vocab 32768 while the benchmark runs 8192 -- and the realised memory growth was +139%, not the +60% that clause anticipated. The result says nothing about MTP at larger vocabularies, longer budgets, or with a cheaper head; it is a statement about this operating point.
mitigation: blocks_keys refuses further mtp entries at the queue door while this lesson holds, and the four remaining queued MTP runs (R6MTP_P3, R6MTP_P4) are cut rather than run: the effect is 30x the noise band and reproduced on swapped slots, so four more runs would buy nothing. The broader rule the campaign should carry forward is that any mechanism adding a full-width logits pass must be screened on STEP COUNT before it is screened on val_bpb -- throughput is the binding constraint at this budget, and a mechanism that halves the step count cannot be rescued by being right.
observation: Multi-token prediction at weight 0.1 (zero-initialised mtp_proj into the shared lm_head, t+2 auxiliary cross-entropy) is 0.079484 WORSE in val_bpb than its yoked control, measured over two waves on swapped slots with deltas agreeing to 4e-4 (+0.079681, +0.079288) -- about 30x the largest slot offset ever measured on this host. The mechanism ENGAGED: mtp_aux_loss_drop read 1.967261 against an activation threshold of 0.1, so the auxiliary head demonstrably learned, and this is a valid negative rather than a non-activation. The cost is throughput and nothing else. The treatment ran at 834ms per step against the control's 300ms (2.8x), completed 371 steps against 1011, reached only epoch 1 against the control's 2, and reserved 107536.1 MB of VRAM against 45060.2 (+139%).

applies_when: any activation rule whose predicate describes a two-sided departure, or whose diagnostic is constant across runs. Retire when the queue door checks that at least one TREATMENT satisfies the rule, not only that controls fail it.
diagnosis: An activation rule is prose and a machine-checkable predicate at once, and nothing verifies they agree. The queue door checks that a rule DISCRIMINATES against the control corpus, which lt 0.1 did -- 54 of 54 controls fail it -- so a rule that no TREATMENT can satisfy passes the door untouched. Discrimination was tested in one direction only. A second, quieter defect sits underneath: secmom_ortho_ratio is identical to eight decimals across every run that emits it (15.08494568 in all five precond treatments, 0.4858 in all controls), so it is shape-determined rather than measured. It can show the code path differs but cannot detect a run-specific failure to engage, which is what an activation diagnostic is for. secmom_max, by contrast, varies run to run (17.31 to 27.22 against 0.24 to 0.28).
mitigation: hyp_stack_transfers_to_tbs18_r6_v3 uses secmom_max gt 1.0, which is one-sided by construction, varies run to run, and was validated as discriminating (60 of 60 controls fail) BEFORE this result existed rather than chosen to fit it. The correction is post hoc and is recorded as such: it is defensible only because the same 15.08494568 appears in the R4X quad measured hours earlier, so the rule was already unsatisfiable then and would be equally wrong had this run come back terrible. The structural fix, not yet built, is for claims.diagnostic_would_discriminate to require evidence that some TREATMENT can satisfy the rule -- today it only proves controls fail it, which is half a check.
observation: hyp_stack_transfers_to_tbs18_r6_v2 declared activation as secmom_ortho_ratio lt 0.1. The treatment read 15.08494568 and E3 refused R6XF_P1_s0_treat as INCONCLUSIVE -- on val_bpb 0.981536, the best result the campaign has produced. The rule was backwards: an orthogonalized matrix has entries of order 1/sqrt(max(A,B)), about 0.044 at this width, so a second moment tracking the POLAR OUTPUT sits near that reference (control 0.48584709) while the reorder makes it track RAW MOMENTUM on a larger scale (treatment 15.08494568), a 31x separation UPWARD. The predicate TEXT inherited from hyp_precond_pre_r1_v2 said the statistic must 'depart from 1 by an order of magnitude', which is two-sided; the encoded rule captured only the downward half. Intent and encoding disagreed and the encoding is what ran.

applies_when: any liveness or capacity claim derived from matching a pattern against process command lines, especially over ssh where the transport carries the pattern.
diagnosis: A pattern-matched liveness check can match the act of asking. This is the same failure as pooling gpu:-1 as a device: a measurement that includes the observer. The campaign already had a rule about owner-filtering process checks, and it was satisfied -- the processes WERE ours -- which is why owner-filtering alone did not catch it. The missing property is that the query must not be a member of the set it counts. Note the supervision added to tools/tick.sh was checked against this and does NOT self-match: it returns 0 when no dispatcher runs and 1 when one does, verified by probing with a marker string present only in the querying command.
mitigation: Liveness claims use a bracketed pattern that cannot match the querying shell (`grep "[.]venv/bin/python train\.py"`), or match on the executable path rather than the script name. Any claim about what is running is grounded in that form before it is reported. The general rule, which is what makes this worth a lesson rather than a typo: an instrument must not be a member of the population it measures.
observation: Twice today an ad-hoc `pgrep -f train.py` over ssh returned a positive count with no trainer running, because the remote shell executing the query carried the pattern in its own command line. The first instance produced a false statement to the operator -- 'OUR TRAINERS ARE UP' -- when the process matched was the variant-build subprocess and no run had launched. The second reported 'trainers: 2' while `ps -u zhubaiyu -o args= | grep -c "[.]venv/bin/python train\.py"` returned 0, and would have blocked a dispatcher restart indefinitely.

applies_when: the host's sustained free-GPU count is below the width of the waves being queued. Retire when the box reliably yields four free GPUs.
diagnosis: This is the third instance of the same shape. L043 named a seed gate that could not be satisfied a pocket veto; L047 narrowed L043's own mitigation after it grew a second one; and this is a third, built by me, where the gating EXPERIMENT rather than the criterion was unreachable. The common error is choosing a gate without checking that the thing it waits for can actually happen on the machine in front of us. A quad is the better design -- treatment on every device once, device offset fully cancelled -- and on a box that yields two GPUs it measures nothing at all, which makes the weaker width-2 design strictly better. tools/queue_quad.py has offered --width 2 the whole time, documented as the option for exactly this case, and the queue was built at width 4 anyway.
mitigation: R5MU and R5MC are re-queued at width 2 as R5MU2 and R5MC2, so the adoption gate is reachable. The remaining 12 width-4 waves stay as they are for now and are a known liability rather than a hidden one: they are counted here so the next reader sees 48 runs that cannot start rather than a queue that looks full. Before queueing a wave, check the width against the host's RECENT sustained capacity, not against the design one would prefer.
observation: 56 of 66 pending runs (85%) sat in width-4 waves. The dispatcher has logged 'waiting for 4 free GPUs' since 07:35Z, more than nine hours, and every launch it has made since is 2-wide. The two waves gating tbs=18 adoption under L047 -- R5MU and R5MC -- were among the unrunnable ones, so the adoption gate could not be satisfied by any amount of waiting.

applies_when: the 300-charged-second single-H200 budget, for any implementation that performs a SEPARATE full-vocabulary pass per step in addition to the cross-entropy. NOT covered, and explicitly left open: an implementation that REUSES the logsumexp cross-entropy already computes internally, which could deliver the same regularisation at near-zero marginal cost and is a materially different experiment.
diagnosis: At a fixed 300-second budget on this benchmark, the binding constraint is step count, and the shared cost of both failures is an extra pass over the VOCABULARY dimension every step. MTP adds a second [B,T,V] backward through the head; z-loss adds a chunked logsumexp over [B*T, vocab]. Crucially the z-loss cost is INDEPENDENT OF LAMBDA -- the logsumexp is computed every step whatever the coefficient multiplying it -- so the conventional 1e-4 would pay the identical 3.34x slowdown and the arm would fail for the same reason. The coefficient was never the variable that mattered, which is worth stating because the round originally proposed 1e-4 and the debate was about which coefficient to run.
mitigation: blocks_keys refuses further zloss entries while this holds. The forward-looking rule, now supported by two independent measurements rather than one: screen any proposed mechanism on whether it adds a vocabulary-width pass BEFORE screening it on val_bpb, and if it does, require an implementation that shares the existing pass. The corrected diagnostic is itself evidence this instrument now works -- logz_sq_mean, the statistic the generator emitted before today, reads 1.516097 and would have FAILED the same 1.0 threshold that logz_sq_final passes at 0.163344, so the run would have been recorded as a non-activation and the finding lost.
observation: z-loss at lambda=0.1 measured +0.146910 against its yoked control (1.138373 vs 0.991463), 303 steps against 1012, MFU 12.34 against 42.27, epoch 1 against 2. Activation CONFIRMED on the corrected diagnostic: logz_sq_final 0.163344 is below the 1.0 threshold, so the regulariser genuinely bound the partition function, and the degeneracy companion zloss_frac_of_total 0.037858 shows it did not swallow the objective. This is the second mechanism in one day killed by the same cause: MTP measured +0.079484 with its auxiliary head demonstrably learning (mtp_aux_loss_drop 1.967261). Both worked exactly as designed and both lost on throughput alone.

applies_when: any claim that two interventions failed for a common cause. Retire when a FLOPs-matched non-vocabulary arm has separated generic compute cost from the vocabulary-pass explanation.
diagnosis: Roughly half of z-loss's harm is NOT throughput. The most likely remaining cause is the coefficient itself: lambda=0.1 is a thousand times the conventional 1e-4, taken from a source that reports it as optimal at a scale this benchmark does not share, and a penalty that strong on log Z plausibly distorts training directly rather than merely costing time. I did not check this before generalising. The two arms were both large, both negative, and both slow, and 'both add a vocabulary pass' was a tidy story that fit -- so I wrote the screening rule without running the one arithmetic check that would have tested it. A round critic ran it and the story did not survive. Note this cuts against a decision I made earlier the same day: the round originally proposed lambda=1e-4 and I overrode it to 0.1 to match the registered hypothesis. The override was correct PROCEDURE -- a cfg must match the hypothesis it cites, or E4 refuses it -- and it now looks like the scientifically weaker choice, which is an argument for registering a hypothesis at the coefficient you actually want rather than for loosening the rule.
mitigation: L053's screening rule survives in weakened form: a vocabulary-width pass is a strong PRIOR against a mechanism at this budget, not an explanation of its full effect, and the step-law residual must be computed before any common-cause claim is written down. The block on zloss stands on the measurement, but its scope is now explicit -- the arm that failed was lambda=0.1 with a SEPARATE logsumexp, and BOTH the coefficient and the extra pass are candidate causes with roughly equal shares. The right follow-up is therefore two arms, not one: a fused implementation reusing the cross-entropy's internal logsumexp, run at the conventional 1e-4, plus a weight-0 fused arm to price the manual-kernel cost against F.cross_entropy. A FLOPs-matched non-vocabulary decoy, proposed by critic-7, would separate 'vocabulary pass' from 'generic added compute' and is the cheapest decisive test of what remains of L053.
observation: L053 claimed MTP and z-loss failed for the SAME reason -- each adds a vocabulary-width pass per step, costing step count -- and generalised that into a screening rule. Applying the campaign's own step law (-0.05974 bpb per e-fold, valid here because tokens_per_step is 524288 in every arm so the fit and the application share an operating point) shows the story is only half right. MTP loses 1.0025 e-folds of steps, predicting +0.059889 against an actual +0.079681, a residual of +0.019792. z-loss loses 1.2060 e-folds, predicting +0.072044 against an actual +0.146910, a residual of +0.074866. The residuals replicate almost exactly on the swapped slots (+0.019856 and +0.074674), so the difference is structural and not noise. Step count explains 75% of MTP's damage and only 49% of z-loss's.
sibling_search: Checked every other multi-arm generalisation in the lessons file for the same untested-common-cause shape. L049 (MTP alone) claims only throughput and its 75% step-law coverage supports that. L040 (tbs=20) and L042 (three-lever stack) each rest on a single mechanism, so there is no common-cause claim to test. This is the only instance.

applies_when: any statistic is quoted from a tool or from prose rather than recomputed, and whenever a fitted law is applied outside the range it was fitted on.
diagnosis: The common thread is quoting a number without owning its derivation. The MTP figure was a stale mean carried forward after a third pair landed. The t came from a tool and was repeated without asking what its degrees of freedom were. The step law was PROSE: it had been quoted for hours, used to argue that two mechanisms shared a cause, and no code implemented it, so nobody -- including the operator who used it -- could check whether it was fitted on controls or on everything, at one operating point or across three. Two independent Fable critics found the same two arithmetic errors, which is a sign they were discoverable rather than subtle. What SURVIVES all three corrections is the qualitative claim of L054: z-loss's unexplained residual is +0.064644 against MTP's +0.011294, a factor of 5.7, and the direction holds under every step-law value the campaign has used. A NEW caveat neither the operator nor the critics stated: the control fit spans 621 to 1020 steps while the arms it judges ran 303 to 372, so every one of these shares is an EXTRAPOLATION below the fitted range.
mitigation: direction.step_law() now fits the law from CONTROLS ONLY at a single tokens_per_step, so no treatment can influence the law that judges it and the operating point is shared by construction. direction.step_law_explains() returns None when two arms differ in tokens_per_step -- applying it across that boundary is forbidden here, and returning a number anyway is how a prose rule gets ignored -- and it sets an `extrapolated` flag when the arm's step count falls outside the fitted range, which is TRUE for both of today's results. Quote effects against the measured band, not against a t computed on one degree of freedom.
observation: Three numbers the operator reported today do not survive recomputation. (1) MTP was quoted as +0.079484 'across three replicates'; +0.079484 is the TWO-pair mean and the three deltas are +0.079681, +0.079288 and +0.079131, giving +0.079367. (2) z-loss was quoted at t=2110.7, taken from tools/verdict.py's same-GPU re-pairing, which compresses sd from 0.000303 to 0.000098; the raw within-wave pairing gives t=683.9, and BOTH are df=1 on two pairs, where any t is arithmetic rather than evidence. (3) L054 claimed the step law explains 75% of MTP's damage and 49% of z-loss's, using a slope of -0.05974 that exists nowhere in code. Refitting on CONTROLS ONLY at a single tokens_per_step of 524288, n=84, gives -0.06822 -- close to L006's -0.0687 and not -0.05974 -- under which the shares are 86% and 56%.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for other fitted constants quoted without a fit: found the noise band and the device resolution, both of which ARE computed in code (direction.noise_band, direction.device_resolution) and take their population from the corpus. The step law was the only unimplemented one. Also checked every lesson quoting a step law -- L005 uses 0.063, L006 uses 0.0687, L018 and L020 quote it qualitatively -- so the value has drifted across records, which is the same defect in the documentation layer.

applies_when: the trainer host is shared and a tenant cycles rather than departing. Retire when a device's burn count has been observed to decay to zero over a full campaign day without a repeat.
diagnosis: The early-release rule read the wrong evidence. Eight minutes without a compute app shows a tenant has PAUSED; on that timescale an intermittent job is indistinguishable from a departed one. The dispatcher fix shipped in 8568b99 -- the clean window now doubles per burn a device has caused, and the counts persist across restarts -- but shipping a fix is not the same as recording the failure, and this campaign's own rule is that every invalid run becomes a typed lesson or the cost is paid twice. An independent process audit found these four as the only uncovered failures on the board, which is also the answer to whether the rule is being followed by habit: it was not.
mitigation: Recorded rather than re-fixed: 8568b99 already carries the code change. The operational consequence worth carrying forward is that a replication wave launched onto a recently-burned device is worth LESS than the same wave launched elsewhere, because its expected loss rate is higher -- so when capacity allows a choice, replication of a headline result should go to the devices with the lowest burn counts, not merely to whichever two are free first.
observation: Four runs were invalidated by co-tenancy and never turned into a lesson: R6XF_P2_s0_ctrl, R6XF_P2_s1_treat, R6XF_P3_s0_ctrl and R6XF_P3_s1_treat. They are not incidental failures -- they are precisely the replication of R6XF_P1, whose val_bpb 0.981536 is the best the campaign has recorded, so their loss is why that result still rests on ONE valid pair. The contamination is visible in the numbers: the P2 control read 1.031001 at 781 steps and the P3 control 1.004891 at 823, against P1's clean 0.991679 at 1011. Both waves were launched onto devices whose quarantine had been lifted early on eight minutes of quiet, and the tenant returned 35 seconds after the P3 launch.
sibling_search: Searched for other places the campaign trusts a quiet interval as evidence of absence. host/dispatch.py had exactly two: the early quarantine release (fixed, now exponential in burn count) and MINFREE_MB, which reads instantaneous free memory when CLAIMING a device -- that one is a point measurement with no interval assumption, so it is not a sibling. tools/health.py treats a 30-minute staleness window as degraded rather than as proof of absence, which is the correct direction. Also re-checked every ok:false run in runs/sweep/results for other uncovered failures: 12 invalid runs total, and after this lesson all 12 map to a registered lesson (L002, L018, L023, L056).

applies_when: a hypothesis names a cfg key. Retire when every registered hypothesis has been shown to build a variant that differs from the control.
diagnosis: build() already refused a registered MECHANISM with no branch -- a guard written for exactly this failure -- but that check enumerates keys the policy knows, so a key the policy has never heard of slipped past it. The consequence is worse than an unrunnable experiment: a round could spend a proposal on one, and only the byte-identical check at the queue door would catch it, after the reasoning had already been done. Three independent reviewers reached counts of nine, ten and ten, which is a fair signal the defect was sitting in plain sight. The practical effect is that the campaign's shortage of runnable NEW mechanisms was largely self-inflicted: the registry looked far richer than it was, so 'what should we test next' kept returning ideas that could not be built.
mitigation: make_variant.build() now raises on any cfg key outside KNOB_AXES and MECHANISMS, with a message that says implement the knob or stop citing it. A paired test asserts an unknown key is refused AND that a known knob still builds. The ten hypotheses are left registered rather than deleted: they are legitimate ideas with sources behind them, and the honest state is 'proposed, not yet implementable' rather than 'never existed'. Implementing any of them is now a code task with a named blocker instead of a proposal that silently evaporates.
observation: Ten registered hypotheses name cfg keys that exist in neither direction.KNOB_AXES nor direction.MECHANISMS: hyp_adam_group_warmup_only_r1, hyp_cooldown_adam_floor_r1, hyp_lr_peak_first_exposure_r1, hyp_muon_shape_rule_exact_r1, hyp_beta1_high_variance_groups_r1, hyp_periln_branch_norm_r1, hyp_lmhead_beta1_horizon_r1, hyp_namo_scale_preserving_r1, hyp_kron_byte_input_code_r1 and hyp_muon_output_projections_only_r1. make_variant.build() dropped the unknown key silently and returned the control source byte-for-byte, so every one of them would have produced a control labelled as a treatment. Two further hypotheses declare activation diagnostics no generated line emits (hyp_qk_norm_instrument_r1 declares qk_prenorm_rms_logdev; hyp_wd_zero_on_muon_matrices_r1 declares wd_delivered_total).
sibling_search: The same shape is 'a guard that enumerates the known and therefore cannot see the unknown'. Searched for other enumerate-the-known checks: direction.is_platform already fails SAFE on any unrecognised key, which is the correct polarity and is documented as such in CLAUDE.md; claims.blocked_values iterates the lesson's keys rather than the cfg's, so an unknown key is simply unblocked, which is right because a lesson can only forbid what it named; coe.e4_method_code compares generated bytes and so is key-agnostic by construction. build() was the only one whose enumeration produced a SILENT pass. Also re-ran the check across all 60 registered hypotheses rather than only the ten named by reviewers, confirming the count.

applies_when: any analysis derives a run's identity or grouping from the queue rather than from the result record.
diagnosis: The queue is a plan and the result is evidence, and the analysis was reading the plan. That makes evidence retroactively deletable by an ordinary housekeeping action -- cutting redundant queue entries, which this campaign does routinely and did four times today. The failure is silent by construction: a dropped arm looks exactly like an arm that never ran. Worse, recovering the run from its NAME was not sufficient on its own, because the variant hash also came from the queue, so the recovered arm grouped separately from its own wave-mates and appeared as a lone unusable block.
mitigation: The wave is taken from the result if it carries one, then the queue, then parsed from the run NAME, which queue_quad builds as <wave>_s<slot>_<role>; the variant hash falls back to REBUILDING it from the result's own cfg, which is a pure function of that cfg and needs no queue at all. host/dispatch.py now writes wave_group into every result record, so the fallbacks are a safety net rather than the mechanism. verdict.py PRINTS a note naming any run it recovered this way, because a silent recovery is only marginally better than a silent loss.
observation: tools/verdict.py resolved a run's wave_group and variant hash ONLY through runs/sweep/queue.json. R6MTP_P3 ran to completion and its result was written; the queue entry was then cut as redundant, and the verdict silently reverted to reporting two MTP pairs (+0.079484) while the campaign reported three (+0.079367). No warning was printed. A reproducibility audit found the discrepancy from outside the tool and reported the campaign's number as unreproducible -- correctly, though the campaign's number was the right one and the tool was wrong. With the fix the raw within-wave mean over three pairs is +0.079367 (sd 0.000283, df=2), matching what was claimed.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for every read of queue.json in an analysis path. Found four: verdict.py (both defects, fixed here), decide.py and balance.py (both read the queue to rank or classify PENDING work, which is the queue's proper job and not an evidence path), and coe.py e4_method_code, which reads the queue to check a variant matches its hypothesis -- that one is about a QUEUED entry and is correct. analyze.py and direction.py read results only. So verdict.py was the sole analysis path resolving evidence through the plan.

applies_when: any change to direction.PLATFORM, since is_platform() matches exactly and therefore redefines the entire control corpus at once.
diagnosis: The adoption cost was described in earlier rounds as 'the control corpus is retired and must be recalibrated', which sounds like a bill to be paid afterwards. It is not: between the moment PLATFORM changes and the moment new controls land, the instrument reads nothing at all, and any wave launched in that window is unmeasurable. The ordering is the whole content of the cost and it had been stated in a way that hid it. Three rounds discussed this adoption and none of them counted the controls.
mitigation: RECAL18, eight runs at exactly the proposed platform config, is queued NOW. They are treatments under the current platform and become the control corpus the instant PLATFORM changes, so the instrument is ready at the moment of adoption rather than restored some time after it. Adoption proceeds when RECAL18 has landed and its within-GPU sd is comparable in scale to the 0.000189 residual sd measured at tbs=19; if it is not, the resolution model does not transfer and every verdict at the new platform needs a wider band before it is trusted. Adoption takes tbs=18 ALONE: the ve/swdiv/precond bundle rests on R6XF's single valid pair, whose two replications were destroyed by a cycling tenant (L056), and bundling an unreplicated three-lever stack into the definition of 'control' would make every future verdict depend on it.
observation: L047's adoption gate is satisfied: R5MU2 landed at raw -0.007498 over three pairs and R5MC2 at raw -0.005221 over three, both counterbalanced and both at epoch 2.0 with no regime shift. Adoption was nonetheless NOT performed, on a fact that no prior round had checked: changing direction.PLATFORM's tbs from 19 to 18 drops the control corpus from 90 valid runs to 4, because is_platform() defines a control by exact config match and every one of the 90 sits at tbs=19. Four controls cannot support per-device means across four devices, a within-wave noise band, or the device resolution that every verdict is measured against.

applies_when: any queue entry names an artifact the dispatcher must open at launch, and whenever entries are added by any path other than tools/queue_quad.py.
diagnosis: Two independent faults. The operator's: bypassing queue_quad meant bypassing every check it performs -- it builds the variant, ships it, verifies the edit applied, refuses a cfg identical to the control and refuses an uncounterbalanced arm. Hand-writing the entry got the one field wrong that queue_quad would never have got wrong, which is the argument for the tool rather than against it. The dispatcher's, and the more serious one: a missing file is a PERMANENT condition. Retrying it cannot succeed, and the retry loop is not free -- it re-claims and releases real GPUs on every poll and buries the log. The dispatcher already distinguishes a transient condition from a permanent one for waves that can never assemble (WAVE WEDGED); launch failures had no such distinction.
mitigation: The dispatcher now counts identical launch failures per entry, logs at most LAUNCH_FAIL_MAX=3 of them, prints one LAUNCH BLOCKED line naming the likely cause, and stops attempting that entry. The entry STAYS QUEUED and becomes launchable the moment the missing artifact is shipped, because the operator's real fix is to ship the file rather than to requeue the work. The operator-side rule is simpler: add queue entries through queue_quad, which builds and ships the variant as part of queueing, and never by editing queue.json directly.
observation: Eight RECAL18 queue entries were hand-written directly into queue.json rather than built through tools/queue_quad.py, and their 'variant' field carried a bare hash ('50ceed0a255d') where every real entry carries a filename ('0f3e2d0c166c.py'). The dispatcher could not open the file and logged LAUNCH FAILED, then retried on the next poll, and the next: more than thirty identical failures in three minutes, each one claiming and releasing two GPUs, while a queue of perfectly launchable waves sat behind it. The variant file itself existed on the host the whole time; only the suffix was missing.
sibling_search: Grepped host/dispatch.py for every other unbounded retry on a per-poll path. Found three: the co-tenancy scan and the quarantine sweep both re-evaluate cheap in-memory state and are correct to run every poll; the WAVE SPLIT branch already tombstones or reports WEDGED once via the _WEDGED set, which is the pattern copied here. Also checked tools/tick.sh, which reports rather than retries. The launch path was the only unbounded one. Separately grepped runs/sweep/queue.json for other entries whose 'variant' lacks a .py suffix: none besides the eight fixed here.

applies_when: the tbs=18 operating point, which is now the platform. Retire when the platform moves again.
diagnosis: The recalibration-before-adoption ordering worked exactly as L059 argued: because the eight runs were queued at the proposed config while the old platform was still current, they were treatments on Tuesday and the control corpus on Wednesday, and the instrument was never blind. Adoption exposed one stale constant immediately -- direction.step_law() defaulted tokens_per_step to 524288, the value the platform had on the day the function was written, so the law returned None the moment the platform moved. That is a bug with a delayed fuse and the campaign has now shipped several of the same shape. Two limits on the new instrument are worth stating rather than discovering later: the step law is now fitted over a 1938-2006 step range, far narrower than the 621-1020 it spanned at tbs=19, so almost any treatment that changes throughput will be flagged as extrapolating; and eight of the twelve controls sit on gpu6 and gpu7, the only devices available for hours, so the gpu4 and gpu5 means rest on two runs each.
mitigation: step_law() now derives its operating point from PLATFORM rather than a literal. Adoption took tbs=18 ALONE: the ve/swdiv/precond bundle still rests on R6XF's single valid pair, and putting an unreplicated three-lever stack into the definition of a control would make every future verdict depend on it. Every effect measured before this point was measured against a tbs=19 baseline and stays valid on its own terms; effects measured after it are against a baseline 0.0075 lower, and the two must not be pooled. The narrow step-law range is the reason step_law_explains() returns an extrapolation flag, and verdict.py prints it.
observation: direction.PLATFORM's tbs moved from 19 to 18 after RECAL18 landed eight runs at exactly the proposed config. The falsifier stated in L059 did not fire, and the instrument improved rather than degrading: pooled within-GPU sd is 0.000079 against 0.000189 at tbs=19 (0.42x), and the device spread is 0.000427 against 0.000489. The control corpus is 12 runs with per-device means on all four GPUs (gpu4 0.985558, gpu5 0.984733, gpu6 0.984211, gpu7 0.983823). The measured noise band fell from 0.00219 to 0.000604. The campaign's baseline val_bpb is now 0.984205 rather than roughly 0.9917.

applies_when: any change to direction.PLATFORM while waves are queued. Retire when adoption is gated on an empty or rebuilt queue by construction.
diagnosis: L043 stated this exact risk in its own mitigation -- that PLATFORM defines 'control' for is_platform and that adoption should therefore land at a clean boundary rather than mid-queue -- and I adopted mid-queue without checking what was in flight. The recalibration question (L059) had absorbed all the attention: I verified the control CORPUS would survive adoption and never asked what adoption would do to the QUEUE. Those are two different populations and only one of them was counted. Adoption itself was correct and the instrument improved; the omission was entirely in the sequencing of the work already queued behind it.
mitigation: All 42 unrun entries in the six families were cut and rebuilt against the adopted platform, which also simplified them: arms that carried an explicit tbs=19 alongside their treatment key are now single-factor arms, and R6XF -- the four-factor stack whose single valid pair is why 0.981536 was never promoted -- is rebuilt as R7XF, a clean THREE-lever arm against a tbs=18 control. Adoption made that experiment better rather than merely compatible. The forward rule: a PLATFORM change must be accompanied by a queue rebuild in the same operation, because the queue is built against the platform current at queueing time and nothing revalidates it afterwards.
observation: Adopting tbs=18 into direction.PLATFORM orphaned 21 pending control entries across six wave families (R5DBS2, R5MLP2, R5NOQK2, R5S162, R5T172, R6XF). Every one had been built with a tbs=19 control, so after adoption is_platform() no longer recognised it. tools/verdict.py identifies a wave's control by is_platform, so each of those waves would have produced zero controls and two treatments and returned no verdict at all. R5NOQK2_P1 ran before this was noticed: its 'control' completed 1011 steps at 0.991518, which is the retired baseline, against a platform whose controls now run about 2000 steps at 0.984205.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for everything else keyed on is_platform, since anything that classifies a run by comparison to PLATFORM has the same exposure to a platform change. Found five: verdict.py (control identification, the defect here), direction.device_means and direction.step_law (both consume only RESULTS, and the old-platform results simply stop being controls, which is correct), balance.py and selector.py (both skip platform runs when computing effects, also correct), and agenda.py (classifies pending work, so it re-classifies automatically). verdict.py's use was the only one where a platform change silently broke a QUEUED comparison rather than re-partitioning finished evidence.

applies_when: the tbs=19 operating point at which it was measured. Whether it transfers to tbs=18 is exactly what R7NOQK tests; do not assume it does.
diagnosis: This is the campaign's first large negative that is NOT throughput-mediated, and it is the cleanest evidence so far that the benchmark is not purely step-count-limited. MTP and z-loss both lost by spending steps; this arm bought about 40 extra steps and gave back 0.008 bpb anyway, so the damage is to what each step achieves rather than to how many there are. Applying the step law makes the finding stronger rather than weaker: the extra steps should have been worth roughly 0.002 in the treatment's favour, so the quality cost is larger than the raw delta shows. The two pairs were run at the retired tbs=19 baseline and were orphaned by the adoption (L062) -- verdict.py cannot express them, because neither arm is a platform control any more -- so they are recorded here rather than lost, and R7NOQK will measure the same mechanism at the adopted platform.
mitigation: Recorded as a measurement at a retired baseline, with its limits stated: two pairs, one operating point, and a tool that can no longer verdict it. The forward value is that it separates the two ways a mechanism can lose here. Every negative before this one lost step count, which made 'screen on throughput first' look like a complete rule; this one shows the rule is necessary and not sufficient, and that an intervention which BUYS throughput can still be worse. R7NOQK repeats it at the adopted platform against a proper control.
observation: Removing QK-norm measured +0.008469 and +0.007495 against yoked controls on swapped slots, mean about +0.008, at the tbs=19 operating point. The mechanism engaged: qk_q_rms_final reads 1.186702 in the treatment against exactly 1.0 in the control, which is what QK-norm pins. Both arms finished at epoch 2.0, so there is no regime shift. Critically the treatment ran MORE steps than its control -- 1044 against 1011, and 1055 against 1004 -- because removing a normalisation is cheaper. It gained throughput and still lost.

applies_when: any activation rule, and with particular force when its predicate describes a departure from a reference value rather than a threshold.
diagnosis: Both rules were two-sided departures ('the statistic must depart from its control value') encoded one-sided. L050 diagnosed that exact shape and named this fix -- require evidence that some treatment can satisfy the rule -- as NOT YET BUILT. It then recurred within the same session, which is the clearest evidence available that writing the diagnosis is not the same as building the check. A first attempt at the fix was itself too loose: it looked at every non-control run, and qk_q_rms_final is emitted by all of them, so a handful reading 0.999999 satisfied 'lt 1.0' by floating-point accident and the backwards rule passed anyway. The question is whether THIS arm can satisfy the rule, which needs the cfg.
mitigation: diagnostic_would_discriminate now takes the cfg, restricts to runs of THAT arm, and refuses when the arm has runs and none satisfies the rule. When no run of the arm has emitted the field it returns UNVERIFIED rather than 'ok', because a permissive answer must not read as a positive -- an audit had flagged the old wording as a false confirmation. Both queue doors pass the cfg. A paired test asserts the original L050 rule is refused and its correction accepted.
observation: claims.diagnostic_would_discriminate verified only that CONTROLS FAIL an activation rule, never that any TREATMENT could satisfy it. Two rules passed that door and were unsatisfiable by construction. The first, recorded in L050, was secmom_ortho_ratio lt 0.1: the reorder moves the statistic UP to 15.08494568 while controls sit near 0.4858, so controls fail the rule and so does every treatment. The second arrived four hours later -- qk_q_rms_final lt 1.0, where removing QK-norm moves the statistic UP to 1.186702 while every control reads exactly 1.0 -- and produced two E3 failures on results that had in fact engaged perfectly.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for every other precondition that validates one side of a comparison. Found three: coe.py e3b discrimination, which shares this function and is therefore fixed by the same change; make_variant.emits_diagnostic, which asks whether the field is printed at all and is one-sided by nature and correctly so; and claims.blocked_values, which tests a forbidden region and has no satisfiable-side to check. Also re-read every activation rule in lit/hypotheses.jsonl for the departure-from-reference shape: secmom_ortho_ratio and qk_q_rms_final are the two instances, both now superseded, and no third exists.

applies_when: any instrument claim computed over a subset of the available corpus, and any config filter written with a subset test rather than equality.
diagnosis: A round critic challenged the claim on a different ground -- that all eight RECAL18 runs landed on gpu6 and gpu7 in one window, so a quiet half-hour could masquerade as a better operating point. That alternative is REFUTED by the corpus: at tbs=19 gpu6 and gpu7 were the NOISIEST of the four devices (sd 0.000210 and 0.000249, against gpu4's 0.000176 and gpu5's 0.000132), and at tbs=18 they are the quietest measured. The devices that tightened are the ones that were worst, which is the opposite of a quiet-pair artifact. What the challenge did establish is thinness: the tbs=18 figure rests on two devices with five runs each, while tbs=19 spans four devices with 13 to 31 runs over many hours, and gpu4 and gpu5 have exactly one tbs=18 control apiece so no within-GPU sd at all. In chasing the challenge I also ran a second check whose filter allowed EXTRA cfg keys, which swept R5MU2 and R5MC2 treatments in as if they were controls and produced 0.001139 -- five times worse than tbs=19. I very nearly retracted a correct claim on the strength of my own buggy check, and caught it only by listing the runs it had matched.
mitigation: The corrected figures are 0.000104 against 0.000196, a ratio of 0.53x, on twelve controls of which only two devices carry a within-GPU sd. The claim to make is that the tbs=18 instrument is at least as tight as tbs=19 and probably tighter, not that it is 0.42x. gpu4 and gpu5 need tbs=18 controls before the device model there is worth anything, and until they exist a wave landing on either has no device mean behind it. Separately: direction.step_law now takes an explicit baseline cfg, because fitting only on is_platform runs meant adoption made the RETIRED operating point unfittable and silently returned None -- which is what made L063's step-law adjustment unreproducible an hour after it was written. With the baseline passed, the retired law refits on 93 controls and L063's figure reproduces exactly: the credit owed to the QK-norm treatment for its extra steps is -0.002191, so the quality cost is +0.010660 against a raw delta of +0.008469.
observation: L061 reported the tbs=18 instrument as 0.42x the tbs=19 sd, from a pooled within-GPU sd of 0.000079. That figure was computed over the eight RECAL18 runs alone -- the runs launched back-to-back in one quiet 32-minute window. Over ALL twelve exact-cfg tbs=18 controls the pooled within-GPU sd is 0.000104 against 0.000196 at tbs=19, a ratio of 0.53x rather than 0.42x. The adoption falsifier still does not fire and the direction of the claim survives, but it was checked on the most favourable available subset and the reported number was too flattering.

applies_when: an activation rule was written as a comparison against a baseline that has since been adopted. Retire when no result cites these three hypotheses.
diagnosis: The diagnostic did not become wrong; the baseline moved out from under it. All three arms were validly activated when they ran, against controls that really did differ on the statistic, and the eleven completed runs behind them are unaffected -- their val_bpb deltas were measured against tbs=19 controls in the same waves and stand on their own terms. What is no longer possible is asking the ACTIVATION question of them, because their intervention is now the platform or contains it: there is no contrast left to demand and no replacement rule that could restore one. A first attempt to handle this narrowed E3b to hypotheses with pending queue entries, which the test suite immediately caught: that would have stopped the guard firing at all, since a bad diagnostic on already-run work is exactly what E3b is for. The designed exemption -- a documented non_activation lesson naming the hypotheses -- is the correct mechanism and requires writing down what is being excused, which is the point.
mitigation: Excused through the documented path rather than by weakening E3b, which stays able to fail on any hypothesis including retired ones. The forward rule is that an activation diagnostic defined as a COMPARISON AGAINST THE PLATFORM has a shelf life ending at the next adoption, so prefer one that is intrinsic to the mechanism -- secmom_max reads 27 against 0.28 whatever the platform is, while tokens_per_step only ever meant 'different from the current baseline'. This is the third distinct way a platform change has broken something today, after orphaned queue controls (L062) and an unfittable retired step law (L065), and all three share the shape: a quantity defined relative to PLATFORM rather than to the mechanism.
observation: Three hypotheses declared activation as 'tokens_per_step lt 524288' to prove their arm had genuinely halved tokens per step: hyp_tbs18_halved_r4, hyp_tbs18_momentum_fraction_held_r5 and hyp_mu_ceil_coscaled_at_tbs18_r5. Against a tbs=19 control that rule discriminated perfectly -- the control sat at 524288 and the treatment at 262144. The moment tbs=18 was adopted into PLATFORM, every control also read 262144, and E3b correctly reported the diagnostic as one the control now passes and as bit-identical across every run citing it.

applies_when: any analysis that resolves a run's ROLE through the current platform rather than through the wave it belonged to.
diagnosis: The underlying error is the one that has now broken four things today: a quantity defined relative to the CURRENT platform rather than to the thing it describes. A wave is a self-contained comparison and carries its own baseline; asking the current platform which member was the control is asking the wrong object. What is lost is the TOOL's ability to re-derive those figures, not the evidence: the runs are on disk, their deltas were computed by hand, and they are preserved in L061, L063 and the commit log. The sign inversion visible on the surviving group is not a defect -- relative to a tbs=18 baseline, tbs=19 really is +0.007953 worse.
mitigation: NOT FIXED, and deliberately so. Two attempts to resolve the role from the run name failed to restore the waves -- something further upstream drops them too -- and I reverted one of those on a misreading, having blamed my own edit for a collapse adoption had caused. Continuing to patch a live analysis tool while chasing a symptom I had already misdiagnosed once is how a subtly wrong number ships. The limitation is written into verdict.py at the exact line, with its scope and the affected waves named. The fix needs the grouping path understood end to end and a test that fails before it passes.
observation: Adopting tbs=18 collapsed tools/verdict.py from many verdict groups to ONE. Every completed wave whose control had been built at tbs=19 lost its control -- is_platform no longer recognises it, so both members read as treatments and the wave drops out. R5MU2, R5MC2 and R5NOQK2 are affected: three counterbalanced pairs each, all already reported. An evidence audit noticed R5MC2 reading '3 of 4 valid pairs' and recomputed it by hand, which is how this surfaced. L062 had caught the same orphaning for QUEUED entries earlier and I fixed only those; the finished waves were orphaned in exactly the same way and I did not check them.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for every use of is_platform in an analysis path, which is the shape at fault. verdict.py resolves ROLE with it -- the defect here. direction.device_means, direction.step_law, balance.sweeps and selector.family_effects all use it to PARTITION finished evidence, where old-platform runs correctly stop counting as controls, and step_law already takes an explicit baseline (L065) so it can still fit the retired point. agenda.py classifies pending work and re-classifies automatically. Role resolution is the only use where the current platform answers a question that belongs to the wave.

applies_when: R7XF has landed with at least two counterbalanced pairs. Retire when that verdict is recorded.
diagnosis: The number is attractive and the campaign has an obvious incentive to find reasons it survives. Pre-registering the retraction condition removes that discretion while the outcome is still unknown, which is the only moment at which pre-registration means anything. R7XF measures the same three levers -- ve=1, swdiv=4, precond=pre -- against a proper tbs=18 control, so it is a cleaner test than the run that produced 0.981536: adoption turned a four-factor arm into a three-factor one and gave it a real baseline.
mitigation: COMMITTED IN ADVANCE, on a synthesis critic's proposal: if R7XF's counterbalanced mean lands INSIDE the measured noise band of 0.000604, the three-lever stack does not transfer to the adopted platform and 0.981536 is RETRACTED permanently -- struck from analyze.py's headline as a campaign best, not merely omitted from the paper. If it lands outside the band with secmom_max above 1.0 and n_ve_layers above 4 confirming both edits active, the stack is real at the new platform and becomes an adoption candidate in its own right, subject to the recalibration ordering L059 established. Either way the single-pair 0.981536 stops being quoted: it is superseded by a counterbalanced number or it is withdrawn.
observation: val_bpb 0.981536 (R6XF_P1_s0_treat) is the lowest this campaign has recorded. It rests on ONE valid pair: its two replications were destroyed by a cycling foreign tenant (L056), and its wave was a four-factor arm measured against a tbs=19 control that adoption has since retired. It has been kept out of the paper and out of every headline claim all day, which was the right call and is not the same as a decision about what happens when the replication lands.

applies_when: any test whose assertion depends on which runs exist in runs/sweep/results.
diagnosis: A test whose truth depends on an experiment not having run yet is not a test of the guard, it is a snapshot of the corpus. It also fails at the worst possible time -- when new evidence arrives -- and it failed silently between the commit that added it and the next full run, which is precisely the window in which I would have read a green suite as licence. The pre-commit hook installed an hour earlier did not catch it either, because the hook only runs on commit and this went red without any commit touching it.
mitigation: The unverified test now uses swdiv=4096 -- an arm that has never been queued and never will be -- so the UNVERIFIED path is stable regardless of what the campaign runs. The general rule: a guard test must construct the state it needs or pick an input the campaign will never produce, never rely on the corpus lacking something. The swdiv=4194304 ladder assertion is the surviving instance of this class and is named here so the next reader finds it before it fires.
observation: The test suite was RED and I did not know. test_activation_precheck_says_unverified_rather_than_ok asserted that the noqknorm arm reports UNVERIFIED because no run of that arm had emitted the diagnostic. That was true when written and false forty minutes later, when R7NOQK_P1 ran and the guard correctly reported '13 of 13 controls FAIL the rule and 1 of 1 non-control run(s) SATISFY it'. The guard was working; my test asserted a TRANSIENT state and expired the moment the campaign produced the very data it was describing.
sibling_search: Grepped tests/ for every assertion keyed on corpus contents. test_guards_fire.py has four: the blocked-value test (tbs=20 is blocked by a lesson, not by data, so it is stable), the selector-refuses-blocked test (same), the swdiv=4 ladder value pinned at -0.002194 (WILL expire if another single-factor swdiv=4 arm runs -- flagged, not yet fixed, and it is a real instance of this class), and the unverified test fixed here. test_chain_of_evidence.py builds its own fixtures and is immune. The step-law tests read the corpus but assert structure rather than values.

applies_when: the tbs=18 platform at 300 charged seconds. QK-norm removal is not worth further GPU time at this operating point; whether it would matter at a different width or depth is untested and not covered.
diagnosis: This is the first result of the campaign measured entirely at one operating point with no cross-platform inference anywhere in the chain: treatment against a genuine platform control, in the same waves, on swapped slots. It confirms L063, which had to be recorded from runs at the retired baseline that verdict.py could not express, and it confirms it LARGER -- +0.010332 here against about +0.008 there. It is also the second independent demonstration that a mechanism can BUY throughput and still lose, which is what reduced 'screen a mechanism on step count first' from a sufficient rule to a necessary one. Two caveats stated rather than buried: the effect is two pairs on two devices, and the step-law credit is flagged EXTRAPOLATED because the treatment ran 2069-2089 steps while the law is fitted over 1938-2006, so that -0.001519 is a directional correction and not a precise one.
mitigation: blocks_keys refuses further noqknorm entries. R7NOQK_P3 launched before this landed and is left to finish rather than killed; its data will only sharpen the estimate. The forward value is the same as L063's and now rests on platform-native evidence: throughput screening is necessary and not sufficient, and an intervention that makes each step CHEAPER can still make each step worse by more than the extra steps are worth.
observation: Removing QK-norm measures +0.010332 at the adopted tbs=18 platform, counterbalanced across gpu6 and gpu7 (deltas +0.010911 and +0.009754 raw, +0.010379 and +0.010286 same-GPU re-paired), both arms at epoch 2.0, about 17x the measured band of 0.000604. Activation is unambiguous on the CORRECTED rule: qk_q_rms_final reads 1.240477 in the treatment against exactly 1.0 in the control, which is the value QK-norm pins. The treatment again ran MORE steps than its control -- 2069 against 2007, and 2089 against 1988 -- so the step law credits it -0.001519 it never collected, leaving a quality cost of +0.012430.

applies_when: any figure the campaign quotes as a headline. Retire when every headline number in the reporting path is printed by a tool.
diagnosis: Identical in shape to L055, where the step law had been quoted for hours with no code behind it. A number that lives only in prose is not a measurement, it is a memory of one, and it goes stale silently -- there is no moment at which anything disagrees with it. The drift here is small and harmless (0.000024 on the baseline), which is precisely why it survived: a large drift would have been noticed, so the failure mode selects for numbers that are wrong by an amount too small to trip anyone's intuition and large enough to matter against a 0.000604 band.
mitigation: analyze.py now prints PLATFORM BASELINE with the control count, the device count, the pooled within-GPU sd and the platform cfg itself, so the number and the configuration it belongs to are read together. The rule this establishes: if the campaign quotes a figure as a headline, a tool prints it -- otherwise the figure is a memory and will drift without ever being contradicted.
observation: The campaign quoted 0.984205 as the adopted platform's baseline all evening -- in lessons, commit messages and reports -- and NO tool printed it. A reproducibility audit recomputed it live and got 0.984181 over 14 controls, with pooled within-GPU sd 0.000098 rather than the 0.000104 also being quoted. Both had drifted as more controls landed, and the stale figures kept being repeated because nothing recomputed them.
sibling_search: Grepped the reporting path for other headline figures quoted in prose without a printing tool. analyze.py prints the best val_bpb, the all-control spread and now the platform baseline; direction.py prints the within-wave band, explore debt and the device resolution; verdict.py prints every effect with both pairings, df and the step-law share. The remaining prose-only figures are the DEVICE MEANS (quoted per-GPU in several lessons, computed by direction.device_means but never printed by any entry point) and the burn counts (host-side only). Neither is a headline the campaign quotes as a result, so both are recorded rather than fixed.

applies_when: any period in which one council is fresh and another is stale. Retire when the cutoff is derived per-council rather than from the oldest artifact.
diagnosis: The freeze is correct in intent: work proposed without fresh review should not reach a GPU. It is wrong in extent, because it keys on an entry's created_at against a cutoff derived from the OLDEST stale council, so work that a CURRENT council did approve is frozen behind a DIFFERENT council's staleness. Today the round council was fresh and the critique council stale, and the critique council's staleness froze entries the round had just authorised. The two councils audit different things -- one proposes experiments, the other audits the apparatus -- and there is no reason a stale apparatus audit should block an experiment a fresh round approved.
