Note also what the freeze does NOT protect: controls are exempt by design, so the instrument keeps running, which is the right call and is why the recalibration block landed during a freeze.
mitigation: NOT changed tonight, and recorded rather than patched, because the same instinct -- fix the freeze quickly because it is costing GPU time -- is what produced the created_at inheritance bypass this afternoon, which an audit then demonstrated was a genuine hole. The correct change is to derive the cutoff PER COUNCIL and freeze an entry only against the council that authorises its kind: a round-proposed experiment against the round council, an apparatus change against the critique council. That is a real change to the gate's semantics and deserves to be made deliberately with a test, not at the end of a long session while watching idle GPUs.
observation: A pipeline audit measured a 117-minute idle gap from 20:19Z to 22:16Z and found the dispatcher's own log attributes it ENTIRELY to the decision cutoff set by a stale council artifact, not to GPU contention. Two GPUs were free and a fully runnable queue was waiting. An earlier audit had already measured about 154 GPU-minutes lost the same way in the preceding three hours, so the governance layer has now cost this campaign roughly four GPU-hours in a single day -- more than every experiment run today consumed.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/gate.py and host/dispatch.py for every consumer of decision_cutoff. gate.py computes it as the age of the OLDEST failing soft check, which is the conflation named here; dispatch.py's runnable() applies it to created_at with a control exemption. tools/tick.sh publishes it. No other consumer. Also checked whether any OTHER pair of independent gates is combined by taking a worst-case: the health check and host-reachable checks are HARD gates that should indeed block everything, and the chain-of-evidence check is genuinely campaign-wide, so the round-versus-critique conflation is the only instance where two independent audits are collapsed into one cutoff.

applies_when: the shared host, whenever a wave is launched onto a device the campaign has not run on recently. Retire when the box is not shared.
diagnosis: The MINFREE_MB claim check is a POINT measurement taken at claim time, and a tenant that arrives afterwards is not excluded by it -- that race is known and is why the co-tenancy detector and quarantine exist downstream. What is new is the consequence. The campaign's mental model of co-tenancy has been 'the run is slower and therefore invalid', which is a graceful degradation: the arm still produces a val_bpb, the co-tenancy flag marks it, and the loss is one wave. An OOM crash produces NOTHING, so a wave loses its member with no data at all and the orphan-member handling in verdict.py is what stands between that and a silently unpaired delta. Notably this was also the first launch onto gpu1 in many hours, so the campaign reached for a device it had no recent occupancy history on.
mitigation: No code change. Every layer did its job: the claim check, the co-tenancy detector, the quarantine, the crash scanner and the honest ok:false record. The operational consequence worth carrying is that a co-tenancy loss is now known to be bimodal -- a degraded-but-present result, or nothing at all -- so a wave launched onto a device with no recent occupancy history carries a higher variance of outcome than the quarantine burn count alone suggests. This is also the FIRST production exercise of the exponential backoff shipped hours ago: gpu1 now carries burn count 1 and needs 16 minutes of quiet rather than 8, and that count survives a dispatcher restart.
observation: R7MLP_P1_s0_treat exited rc=1 with no val_bpb on gpu1, one minute after launch. The log shows torch.OutOfMemoryError: a foreign process (pid 2839900) held 124.41 GiB of the device's 139.80 GiB, leaving our run 15.23 GiB, and it died allocating a 512 MiB buffer. The dispatcher had claimed gpu1 as free, then detected the tenant and quarantined the device -- both checks worked. Every previous co-tenancy in this campaign degraded a run's step count and left a usable-but-invalid result; this one destroyed the run.
sibling_search: Grepped host/dispatch.py for every place a run's outcome is inferred rather than read. _crashed() scans the log for OOM and traceback markers and correctly caught this one; the result writer records ok:false when val_bpb is absent, so the record is honest; parse() returns an empty metrics dict rather than fabricating. verdict.py's odd-member NOTE is what surfaces the resulting unpaired arm. The gap is not in detection -- every layer behaved -- it is that nothing distinguishes 'invalid but measured' from 'destroyed' when counting what a wave cost, which is a reporting nuance rather than a defect.

applies_when: any pre-registered threshold. Retire when every such threshold is expressed as a call rather than a literal.
diagnosis: Same shape as L055 and L071 -- a number quoted from memory rather than computed -- but pointed at the one place it does the most damage. A pre-registration exists to remove discretion after the outcome is known; a pre-registration bound to a stale literal RESTORES that discretion, because when the result lands there is an argument to be had about which number was meant. Worse, the drift ran in the direction that makes retraction less likely: a band of 0.001430 is easier for an effect to clear than 0.000604, so leaving it unfixed would have quietly favoured keeping the campaign's best number. I did not notice; a critic asked which threshold binds and the recomputation fell out of checking.
mitigation: SUPERSEDES L068's threshold, decided BEFORE R7XF lands. The binding test is the DEVICE RESOLUTION scaled to the number of counterbalanced pairings actually obtained -- direction.device_resolution(rows)['resolution_at'](n) -- computed at verdict time, not a literal. That is the quantity a yoked, counterbalanced design actually buys, and it is what verdict.py already compares every quad against; the within-wave band pools across waves and so carries drift that counterbalancing removes. On today's corpus it is 0.000221 at n=2 and 0.000156 at n=4, but the number that binds is whatever the tool returns when R7XF's pairs are in. If R7XF's mean falls inside that, 0.981536 is retracted permanently. The rest of L068 stands unchanged.
observation: L068 pre-registered that val_bpb 0.981536 would be retracted if R7XF's counterbalanced mean landed inside 0.000604. That literal was the within-wave band when L068 was written. It is now 0.001430 -- the band more than doubled as more waves landed -- so the threshold the campaign committed to is not the threshold the instrument reports, and R7XF has not even run yet. A round critic also found the pre-registration left unresolved which of two defensible thresholds binds: the within-wave band, or the device resolution scaled to the number of pairings, currently 0.000221 at n=2 and 0.000156 at n=4.
sibling_search: Grepped lit/lessons.jsonl for other lessons whose mitigation names a numeric threshold a future decision must clear. L040 blocks tbs>=20 on a measured +0.022545 -- a blocking value, not a decision threshold, and stable. L044 and L048 quote marginals as evidence rather than as gates. L059's adoption falsifier named 0.000189 as a comparison scale and was evaluated the same hour, so it never went stale. L068 is the only pre-registration whose threshold had to survive a delay, and it did not.

applies_when: the adopted tbs=18 platform. The three levers were measured together, so this says nothing about their individual contributions -- R9VE1 isolates ve=1 for the first time.
diagnosis: The stack transfers to the adopted platform, and it is SMALLER there: -0.002510 against the -0.004408 measured at tbs=19. That is consistent with the levers overlapping what tbs=18 already delivers rather than with the earlier number having been wrong, and it is why the transfer had to be measured rather than assumed. Per L068's own terms the single-pair 0.981536 stops being quoted either way -- superseded by a counterbalanced number or withdrawn -- and the outcome is SUPERSEDED: 0.981213 is reached by a treatment inside a counterbalanced wave with both activation diagnostics firing, so it rests on evidence of a kind 0.981536 never had. The retraction clause did not fire; recording that plainly matters as much as it would have if it did, because a pre-registration only means something if both branches are honoured.
mitigation: 0.981213 becomes the campaign's best supported number and 0.981536 is retired from quotation as superseded. The stack is now an adoption CANDIDATE at the adopted platform, subject to L059's ordering -- recalibration controls at the proposed config queued BEFORE PLATFORM changes, never after -- and to L062's rule that a platform change carries a queue rebuild in the same operation. It is NOT adopted tonight: two pairs on two devices is thinner than the four-pair evidence that supported tbs=18, and the campaign has just spent a day paying for one adoption's consequences. The next question is decomposition, not adoption: R9VE1 isolates ve=1, which has never been measured outside this stack.
observation: R7XF resolves the pre-registered test of L068 as amended by L074. The three-lever stack (ve=1, swdiv=4, precond=pre) measured against a genuine tbs=18 platform control gives a counterbalanced mean of -0.002510 over two pairs (deltas -0.002018 and -0.003002), against a binding threshold of resolution_at(2)=0.000229 computed at verdict time. It clears by about eleven times. Activation fires on both arms and both diagnostics: secmom_max 28.81229591 and 29.18190002 against a rule of >1.0, n_ve_layers 8.0 against >4. The treatment reached val_bpb 0.981213, which is lower than the 0.981536 the pre-registration was written about.

applies_when: the adopted tbs=18 platform at 300 charged seconds and this width. Whether a narrower MLP pays at a different depth or dim is untested and not covered.
diagnosis: This is the third mechanism today to BUY throughput and lose anyway, after QK-norm removal (+0.010405, about 60 extra steps) and now the largest of them. Together with the two that lost by SPENDING throughput -- MTP and z-loss, each adding a vocabulary-width pass -- the campaign has now measured five mechanisms that move per-step cost in one direction or the other, and every one of them lost. The only interventions that have won are tbs=18, which changes how many updates the same data buys without changing the cost of a step, and the zero-FLOP three-lever stack. The reading is that the benchmark sits near a local optimum in per-step cost at this budget and both directions away from it are expensive, which is a sharper design rule than 'screen a mechanism on throughput' and is what makes the next three queued arms -- ve density, EMA, gradient clipping, all zero-FLOP -- the right ones to run.
mitigation: blocks_keys refuses further mlp entries at this platform. The quality cost is quoted with its extrapolation flag attached, because the step-law credit is read outside the range the law was fitted on and is directional rather than precise -- the raw +0.011907 is the number that stands without qualification. Note this arm reached three pairs rather than four only because R7MLP_P1's treatment was OOM-killed by a foreign tenant (L073); the surviving control from that wave is deliberately not spliced in, per round 9's judgement that a hand-paired orphan is worth less than a clean pairing.
observation: Halving the MLP ratio from 4 to 2 measures +0.011907 raw over three counterbalanced pairs at the adopted platform (deltas +0.011776, +0.011564, +0.012380), same-GPU re-paired +0.011972, all arms at epoch 2.0. The treatment ran about 350 MORE steps than its control every time -- 2344 against 1983, 2357 against 1989, 2338 against 2006 -- because a narrower MLP is cheaper. The step law credits it -0.008256 for those steps, so the quality cost is +0.020032, the largest this campaign has measured. The tool flags that credit EXTRAPOLATED: the treatment ran 2338-2357 steps against a law fitted over roughly 1938-2007.

applies_when: any analysis that groups waves by treatment identity without regard to the baseline each was measured against.
diagnosis: The group key is (label, variant hash), and after the tbs=18 adoption both treatments read as the same delta from the platform -- {ve:1, swdiv:4, precond:pre} -- and build the same variant. So the key cannot distinguish them. What differs is the CONTROL, and the control's cfg is not in the key. This is the same family as L062, L065, L066 and L067: a quantity defined relative to the current platform rather than to the comparison it belongs to. The synthesis critic of critique 11 forecast that more consumers of the mutable PLATFORM global would break on the next adoption; this is one it did not name, found by reading a verdict rather than by prediction.
mitigation: NOT patched tonight, deliberately. The conclusions already drawn are unaffected: the pre-registered R7XF verdict was computed from the R7XF pairs alone by an explicit script, not from this pooled group, and the same-GPU figure the tool reports is itself immune. Patching verdict.py late in a long session is precisely what produced L067's near-miss, where I made the tool worse and reverted on a misdiagnosis. The fix is to include the CONTROL's cfg in the group key so that two waves sharing a treatment but not a baseline are reported separately, and it wants a test that fails before it passes. Until then the raw within-wave mean on any group spanning an adoption must not be quoted; the same-GPU re-paired mean is the one that survives.
observation: tools/verdict.py pools R6XF_P1 into the same group as R7XF_P1/P2/P3. R6XF's treatment was measured against a tbs=19 control and reads -0.010143; the R7XF pairs are measured against tbs=18 platform controls and read -0.002018, -0.003002 and -0.003956. The raw within-wave mean over the pooled group is -0.004780 with sd 0.003662, which is not an estimate of anything: it averages two different comparisons. The same-GPU re-paired figure, -0.002557, is unaffected because it pairs within a device and the cross-baseline arm cannot pair with the others.
sibling_search: Grepped tools/ for every other grouping key. selector.family_effects keys by FAMILY and pools across baselines identically -- same exposure, not yet demonstrated to bite because its inputs are device-corrected effects rather than raw deltas. balance.sweeps keys by axis VALUE, which has the same shape. analyze.py groups nothing. decide.py groups by wave_group, which is baseline-safe by construction. So verdict.py is the demonstrated instance and selector/balance are the untested siblings, named here rather than assumed clean.

applies_when: any generalisation drawn over a set of results. Retire when a claim of this kind is required to name the arms that do NOT fit before it can be registered.
diagnosis: The claim was false when I wrote it and I had the counter-evidence already: swdiv 2->4 measured -0.002194 and 4->8 measured -0.003218, both FLOP-reducing wins by exactly this route, and both are recorded in L048. I had five results in front of me that fit a tidy story and did not check the ones that did not. This is the same error as L053's common-cause story this morning, which a critic overturned by running one arithmetic check I had skipped -- and I repeated it within the same day, on a larger set, having written the lesson about it. What actually discriminates is not the DIRECTION of the per-step cost change but WHAT is removed: cutting attention span (swdiv) wins repeatedly across four rungs; cutting MLP capacity (+0.011907) or QK normalisation (+0.010405) loses badly, and both of those also gained steps. So 'removes work, gains steps' describes both the best and the worst arms of the day, and is not a predictor of anything.
mitigation: L076's measurement stands unchanged: mlp=2 is +0.011907 with a quality cost of +0.020032, and that is the largest measured. What is withdrawn is the generalisation attached to it. The honest replacement, and it is narrower: at this budget, removing ATTENTION SPAN has paid at every rung tested (2->4, 4->8, and now 8->16 pending counterbalancing), while removing MLP capacity or QK normalisation has lost, and adding a vocabulary-width pass has lost worst. The discriminator is which resource is cut, not whether the step got cheaper. Before registering a cross-arm generalisation, name the arms that do not fit it -- I had two and did not look.
observation: L076 claimed that every mechanism moving per-step cost in either direction had lost, and drew from it that the benchmark sits near a local optimum in per-step cost. R7S16_P1 falsifies it within a single wave, with no pooling required: swdiv=16 measured 0.981347 at 2148 steps against its own yoked control's 0.983755 at 2006 -- an improvement of -0.002408 while GAINING 142 steps. It removes attention FLOPs, runs faster, and is better.
sibling_search: Re-read every lesson registered today that generalises across more than one arm. L053 (vocabulary-width pass) was already corrected by L054 and its surviving form is a prior rather than an explanation. L063 and L070 each generalise from ONE mechanism to the claim that throughput screening is necessary-not-sufficient, which R7S16 supports rather than contradicts. L076 is the only surviving over-generalisation and is corrected here. L072's 'four breakages one shape' was put to an independent synthesist precisely because I distrusted it, and it survived with a falsifiable forecast attached -- which is the standard the others should have met.

applies_when: the shared host, for any device the campaign has not run on within the last hour. Retire if the box's occupancy pattern changes -- verifiable from dispatch.log, where a clean run on gpu1, gpu2, gpu4 or gpu5 would be the evidence.
diagnosis: MINFREE_MB is a point measurement at claim time, so a device reads free in the instant between a tenant's jobs. The inference worth drawing is about WHY those devices were momentarily free: gpu6 and gpu7 appear to be the two nobody else wants, which is why the campaign has had them for hours, and the others are free only in the gaps of somebody's job queue. That makes a launch onto an unfamiliar device closer to a coin flip than to a claim. L073 already said such a wave 'carries a higher variance of outcome'; the strength of the effect is what is new, and it is strong enough to change how replication should be scheduled rather than merely noted.
mitigation: No code change, and deliberately so: the dispatcher's job is to use free capacity and it cannot know a tenant is between jobs. The operational rule is about WHICH work goes where. A wave that RESOLVES a claim -- a replication, a counterbalancing swap, a pre-registered test -- should not be the one sent to an unfamiliar device, because losing it costs a decision rather than a run. Exploratory arms are the right thing to gamble there. Tonight three of the three losses were exactly the wrong kind: a replication, a counterbalancing arm, and a control. The burn counts now persist per device (gpu1, gpu2 and gpu4 each carry 1), so the backoff already lengthens the quiet window each device must show, and this lesson records why that backoff matters more than it looked when it was written.
observation: Three times tonight the dispatcher reached beyond gpu6 and gpu7, and all three were co-tenanted within about a minute of launch: gpu1 at 22:49:28Z (an OOM that destroyed R7MLP_P1_s0_treat outright), gpu4 at 23:46:16Z (R7XF_P4_s0_treat, degraded to 919 steps), and gpu2 at 00:04:39Z (R7S16_P3_s0_ctrl, killed 29 seconds after launch). Meanwhile every wave on gpu6/gpu7 across the same period completed cleanly. Three for three against zero for many.

applies_when: the adopted tbs=18 platform at 300 charged seconds. The swdiv ladder has not saturated -- 8->16 still pays -- so the next rung is a legitimate experiment rather than a knob being turned past its usefulness.
diagnosis: This replaces L078's correction with something quantitative. L076 claimed the direction of the per-step cost change was what mattered and R7S16 falsified it; L078 replaced that with 'which resource is cut', which is a label rather than a mechanism. The actual discriminator is the RATIO of quality cost to throughput credit, and all three FLOP-reducing arms measured today can be read off it: swdiv=16 costs +0.001004 in quality and earns -0.003412 in steps, so it nets a win; mlp=2 costs +0.020032 and earns -0.008256, losing by a wide margin; QK-norm removal costs +0.012430 and earns only -0.001519. The arms are ordered by ratio, not by which subsystem they touch, and that is a rule a proposal can be screened against BEFORE it runs -- estimate the FLOPs saved, estimate the capacity lost, and ask whether the exchange rate is favourable. Every quality-cost figure here carries the tool's EXTRAPOLATED flag, because the treatments ran 2145-2153 steps against a law fitted over roughly 1938-2007, so the ratios are directional and their ordering is the claim rather than their exact values.
mitigation: The swdiv sweep continues; it is the only axis that has paid at every rung. Note the corrected ladder is what kept it alive: before L048 removed a leaked three-lever delta from the attention family, the 4->8 marginal read three times smaller than it was and the sweep looked saturated. Had that attribution bug stood, this rung would never have been queued. That is the clearest case in this campaign of an apparatus repair producing science rather than merely protecting it.
observation: swdiv=16 measures -0.002742 same-GPU paired over three pairings at the adopted platform (raw deltas -0.002408, -0.003184, -0.002300), all arms at epoch 2.0, against a resolution of 0.000219 -- about 12.5x. It is the fourth consecutive win on the attention-span axis after 2->4 (-0.002194), 4->8 (-0.003218) and the stack. The step law explains 142% of it: the roughly 145 extra steps it buys should have been worth -0.003412 and only -0.002742 materialised, so swdiv=16 carries a small quality COST of +0.001004 and wins because the throughput it buys is worth more than the quality it gives up.

applies_when: the adopted tbs=18 platform. The margin is small enough that a different host load could move it either side of the resolution.
diagnosis: This is the mirror image of swdiv=16 under L080's ratio rule: swdiv buys steps worth more than the quality it costs, dbs=64 costs steps worth more than the quality it buys. Both are small, and dbs=64's is small enough that the honest verdict is MARGINAL rather than harmful -- 2.6x resolution on a same-GPU pairing whose df is 1, with a raw pairing that does not reach significance. What it does settle is a confound: dbs and tbs moved together in the R5T17 arm, and micro-batch alone is now shown to do very little on its own, so the tokens-per-step lever is not secretly a micro-batch lever. That is the question this arm was queued to answer and it answers it cleanly even though the effect itself is marginal.
mitigation: Reported as MARGINAL, not as a harm. Quoting +0.000552 as a result would overstate it: the same-GPU figure rests on df=1 and the raw pairing gives t=1.6. The durable content is the deconfounding -- micro-batch alone does very little, so tbs=18's benefit is not a micro-batch effect in disguise -- plus a clean demonstration that raw cross-GPU deltas can look like a treatment effect when they are a device effect, which is why L020's same-GPU re-pairing exists and why verdict.py prints BOTH pairings with their degrees of freedom.
observation: Halving the micro-batch to dbs=64 at the adopted platform measures +0.000552 same-GPU paired over four pairings, against a resolution of 0.000209 -- about 2.6x, the smallest margin of any arm measured today. The raw within-wave mean is +0.000507 with t=1.6 at df=3, which does not clear its own dispersion. The raw deltas split cleanly by device: the two waves with the treatment on gpu5 read +0.000945 and +0.001130, the two on gpu6 read -0.000022 and -0.000026. That is not a treatment-by-device interaction, it is gpu5 being the slower device -- a treatment there loses more steps -- and it is precisely what same-GPU re-pairing removes. The step law, and this is the FIRST arm today where it is INTERPOLATED rather than extrapolated (treatments ran 1936-1958 steps against a law fitted over 1938-2007), explains 132%: the step loss should have cost +0.001246 and only +0.000552 materialised, so dbs=64 slightly IMPROVES per-step quality by -0.000301 and loses on throughput.

applies_when: any activation rule whose statistic is computed from tokens_per_step, dbs, or any other platform quantity. Retire when such rules are expressed relative to the control's own reading rather than as an absolute threshold.
diagnosis: Sixth instance of the family L072 named and forecast: a quantity defined relative to the current platform rather than to the thing it describes. The five before were orphaned queue controls (L062), an unfittable retired step law (L065), three vacuous tokens_per_step diagnostics (L066), orphaned completed waves (L067) and verdict.py pooling waves across baselines (L077). The forecast said more PLATFORM consumers would break; this is one it did not name specifically, and it is the first to surface from a routine result rather than from an audit. What is genuinely new is HOW it surfaced: claims.diagnostic_would_discriminate REFUSED the rule on the grounds that all four non-control runs also fail it -- the check built this afternoon under L064, catching a live defect before I had diagnosed it. Every previous instance today was found by an agent or by me after the fact.
mitigation: hyp_dbs64_alone_r5_p18_v2 uses grad_accum ge 2.0 -- 31 of 31 controls fail it, 4 of 4 treatments satisfy it -- with a post_hoc_rule_change field recording that the correction is arithmetic rather than outcome-driven, and a predicate stating explicitly that the values are platform-dependent and must be restated at the next adoption. L081's conclusion is unchanged: the mechanism engaged, the arm is MARGINAL at +0.000552, and the deconfounding it was queued for stands. The general fix, not built, is to express such rules relative to the control's own reading rather than as an absolute threshold, which would survive any adoption.
observation: The dbs=64 arm declared activation as grad_accum gt 2.0. That discriminated at tbs=19, where the arm read 4.0 against a control's 2.0. Adopting tbs=18 halved both to 2.0 and 1.0, so no treatment could satisfy the rule and E3 marked all four R7DBS treatments INCONCLUSIVE -- on an arm whose mechanism had engaged with a clean 2x separation. grad_accum is tokens_per_step/(dbs*seq_len), so the adoption halved it by arithmetic.
sibling_search: Grepped every registered hypothesis's activation diagnostic for statistics derived from platform quantities. grad_accum (this one) and tokens_per_step (L066's three) are the two that scale with tbs. n_ve_layers, secmom_max, secmom_ortho_ratio, qk_q_rms_final, flops_per_token_M, logz_sq_final, mtp_aux_loss_drop, ema_updates and clip_fired_frac are all intrinsic to their mechanism and unaffected by a platform change -- flops_per_token_M would shift if depth or dim moved, but not with tbs. So the exposure is exactly the two tbs-derived statistics, both now corrected.

applies_when: the 300-charged-second budget on this host with the frozen prepare.py. A different data volume or a longer budget would move where the two costs balance.
diagnosis: The mechanism at the two ends is opposite and the verdict line used to assert the wrong one. tbs=20 and tbs=19 lose by running FEWER optimizer updates over the same data. tbs=17 loses despite running nearly twice as many, because each step sees half the tokens: 3818 x 131072 is about 500M tokens against the control's 1991 x 262144, about 522M, so it never reaches the second epoch. More updates on less data is not a free trade, and the ladder's minimum is where the two costs balance. This also retires a question the campaign has carried since L045/L046 named six step-indexed quantities moving together with tbs: whatever the decomposition, the OPTIMUM is now bracketed on both sides by measurement rather than inferred from one direction.
mitigation: The tbs axis is closed: both neighbours of the adopted value are measured and worse, so further rungs are not worth GPU time. Separately, the SYSTEMATIC REGIME SHIFT line in verdict.py no longer asserts a cause. It claimed the treatment was 'too slow to reach the boundary', which was true of MTP and z-loss and is FALSE here -- tbs=17 reaches epoch 1 while running nearly twice the steps. Same observation, opposite mechanism. The line now reports what was seen and leaves the cause to whoever reads the step counts printed directly above it.
observation: Halving tokens per step again, from the adopted tbs=18 to tbs=17 with dbs=64, measures +0.004153 -- worse -- over two counterbalanced pairs (raw deltas +0.004546 and +0.003761; same-GPU re-paired +0.003889 and +0.004418, both pairings agreeing to six decimal places on the mean). The treatment ran 3818 and 3851 steps against controls at 1991 and 1964, nearly double, and reached only epoch 1.0 against the controls' 2.0. With tbs=20 at +0.022545 and tbs=19 at +0.007953, the ladder now reads: 20 catastrophic, 19 worse, 18 best, 17 worse. The adopted platform sits at the minimum rather than merely being better than where the campaign started.

applies_when: any use of L080's ratio to argue for or against a proposal, until an arm outside the fitting set has tested it.
diagnosis: 'It explains everything I have' is the position L053 was in this morning before a critic ran one arithmetic check and broke it, and it is where I was again when I wrote L080 six hours later. A rule fitted to three points and revised twice against those same three points is a description of them, not a prediction. What makes L080 better than its predecessors is that it is QUANTITATIVE and therefore falsifiable -- but falsifiable is not falsified, and nothing has yet tried. R9VE1 is the first genuine out-of-sample test because ve=1 changes capacity with a near-zero throughput denominator: the ratio is undefined or enormous there, so the rule has to say something specific about an arm structurally unlike the three it was built on.
mitigation: L080's MEASUREMENTS stand; its status is downgraded from finding to IN-SAMPLE HYPOTHESIS until an arm it was not built from tests it. R9VE1 is that test and is already queued. State the prediction before it runs: ve=1 costs almost nothing in throughput, so under the ratio rule its verdict should be decided almost entirely by its quality term and the rule offers no protection either way -- which means a clear ve=1 result neither confirms nor refutes it, and the honest boundary test is an arm with a SMALL but non-zero throughput credit. Also recorded: the three-lever stack has two defensible estimates, -0.002510 as a raw mean (L075) and -0.002557 same-GPU re-paired (L077), and the second is preferable because a pooling defect mixes baselines in the raw group. Cite the estimator, not just the number.
observation: L080 proposed that what decides a FLOP-reducing arm is the RATIO of its quality cost to its throughput credit, and showed swdiv=16 (+0.001004 cost, -0.003412 credit, wins), mlp=2 (+0.020032, -0.008256, loses) and QK-norm removal (+0.012430, -0.001519, loses) ordering cleanly by it. An independent synthesist points out that this is the THIRD formulation of the same pattern in one day -- L076 claimed the direction of the cost change mattered and was falsified within the hour by swdiv=16; L078 replaced it with 'which resource is cut', which is a label rather than a mechanism -- and that all three were fitted to the SAME three arms. The rule explains every arm it was built from and has never been tested against one it did not see.
